517334|2026-03.headline: Motherson posted record Q4 FY26 revenue up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margin up 200 bps, and FY27 capex guided at about INR 6,000 Cr.
517334|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the highest-ever quarterly revenue, growing 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margins up 200 bps YoY, aided by lighting & electronics and aerospace. Normalized PAT rose 66% in Q4, while reported PAT absorbed INR 177 Cr post-tax of European transformation provisions. FY26 revenue crossed INR 1.25 Lakh Cr (+11%), EBITDA margin was 9.5%, and leverage fell to an all-time low of 0.8x. Management flagged copper up about 38% YoY and Middle East-linked crude and polymer inflation, with pass-through recovery expected to lag one or two quarters.

517334|2026-06.headline: Motherson posted record Q1 FY27 revenue, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 26% and margin up 60 bps despite copper, polymer and freight inflation.
517334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 17% YoY and 3% QoQ to a record, and Q1 revenue exceeded Q4 FY26, which management said is unusual since Q1 normally declines sequentially. EBITDA rose 26% YoY with margin up 60 bps, led by the modules and polymer (MPP) business after European restructuring. Normalized PAT grew 55% YoY, with no one-off items in the quarter. Management flagged copper up 40% YoY, polymer prices in Germany up 55% YoY, and the World Container Index up 40% YoY as headwinds, with pass-through lagging by 1-2 quarters. Capex of INR 1,614 crore was in line with the INR 6,000 crore full-year guidance, and leverage fell to 0.8x.

segments.name: Vision systems
segments.commentary: Grew in line with industry; polymer cost inflation in Germany hit the division, but margins were held flat to improving. Management highlighted the mirror business as a high free-cash-flow generator.

qa_highlights.question: What are the annualized revenue and margins for the newly acquired Yutaka and Nexans businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Together they should contribute close to USD 2 billion annualized revenue. Margins are not yet at the industry benchmark of about 11%, but management expects improvement over the midterm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full capex and funding structure for consumer electronics, and how much revenue can 40 million units generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex is about INR 7,500 crore, with the JV partner at 10% equity and Motherson funding 90%. Management declined to give revenue guidance and asked for two more quarters of patience.

qa_highlights.question: How much did commodity headwinds cost in Q1 and how much did restructuring offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. Plastics pass-through is settled periodically, mostly at year-end, so the full effect is expected in Q4. Restructuring benefits are described as meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Why is wiring harness margin impact from copper so small?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the global impact is about 4-5% QoQ with a 3-6 month pass-through lag. The India impact is larger due to rupee depreciation. Diversification and cost actions in international operations offset the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the emerging businesses be separately listed, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said listing is on the cards, possibly within the 5-year plan. Timing depends on execution, and value unlock could come as early as FY28. No firm date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a regulatory tailwind for vision systems from AIS 184 driver drowsiness rules in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajat Jain said new regulations are a tailwind. The Autocruis acquisition brings interior digital mirrors and driver monitoring, subject to homologation in India.

517354|2026-03.headline: Havells' Q4 FY26 was modest: channel stocking for cooling hit by a mild start to summer, while cost inflation from the West Asia war drove calibrated price hikes of 5-20%.
517354|2026-03.overview: Management described a modest Q4 with cooling-product channel stocking hit by a milder start to the season, while industrial and infrastructure-linked categories stayed strong and consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment. Cables and wires volume grew 6% YoY, with value up 14%, helped by copper and aluminium inventory gains and an approximately 8% blended price increase. Margins held except at Lloyd, which was hit by lower revenue, and a Rs 283 crore fair-value gain on the Goldi Solar investment was booked in other income. Management declined to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance, citing the uncertain war and inflation backdrop.

financial_highlights.metric: Blended cables and wires price increase
Fair value gain on Goldi Solar investment
financial_highlights.change: booked in other income in Q4

financial_highlights.metric: Investment in Goldi Solar during the year

financial_highlights.change: long-term average stated as 30-32%; Q4 flagged as year-end release effect
management said work in progress to restore it

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: Volume grew 6% YoY, with industrial cables growing much faster than domestic wires, which were flat to slightly down after destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base. Margins rose sharply, partly from copper and aluminium inventory gains and year-end adjustments. New capacity is still running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue was broadly flat YoY while contribution margin rose to 37%, which management attributed to year-end releases. The long-term margin range is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

segments.name: Lloyd (cooling and appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 was hit by lower revenue from a delayed summer and channel inventory build; the first half of April was also slow. Price hikes of 8-15% by AC type are being implemented to pass on post-war cost increases. A new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4.

segments.name: Fans and ECD
segments.commentary: Fans degrew in value for the full year, with Q4 hit by BEE-norm pre-stocking in Q3 and seasonality. Management expects better volumes in Q1 FY27 on a low base.

segments.name: Other (Solar)
segments.commentary: Other segment grew about 48% YoY, mainly from solar, and its EBIT margin expanded. Management called solar a sunrise industry and said margins should keep improving with operating leverage, but gave no target.

segments.name: Switchgear
segments.commentary: Contribution margin fell below the roughly 38% level because price increases lagged cost increases. Management said it is striving to return to 38% while balancing market share.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 volume or revenue growth guidance; management said it is too early given month-to-month uncertainty from the war and inflation.
Calibrated price hikes are underway across all categories, ranging from 5% to 20% by product range, with Lloyd AC hikes at 8-15%.
Management expects operating leverage in FY27, with revenue growth ahead of expense growth except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.
Management reiterated a medium-term EBITDA margin improvement of over 2 percentage points.
Channel inventory for Lloyd is expected to normalise by the end of April 2026 as the summer picks up in the south and west and reaches the north.
Major FY27-28 capex goes to cables and wires, about Rs 800 crore this year, plus a new R&D centre over the next 2-2.5 years. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
capex_capacity: Cables and wires: new capacity is running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27. About Rs 800 crore is budgeted this year, mainly for cables and wires.
Lloyd: a new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4 FY26, with a refreshed product portfolio launched. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
Solar: capacity is being built through the Goldi Solar investment (Rs 600 crore this year), and management plans to widen the renewable product range.
Underground cables are an under-invested area that the company is now investing in.
A new R&D centre will absorb a large share of capex over the next 2-2.5 years.
demand_pricing: Cooling demand was delayed by a mild start to the season. The first half of April was slow, but south and west have started well and the north is following.
Industrial and infrastructure-linked categories remained strong, while consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment because of higher costs from West Asia disruptions.
Pricing: management said it had not seen price escalation this steep across categories in recent memory. Price increases are calibrated, and management is balancing pass-through against market share.
Pre-buying happened in March ahead of price hikes, especially in cooling products, which management said was accentuated by the price increases.
Copper prices dipped in February and then rose after the war began. Management said the entire increase seen is post-war.

Management said the company is retaining market share in all categories and denied losing share in any category. It said fans, ACs and air coolers degrew for the full year, and it does not disclose product-wise volumes.
Management said a large cement company's entry into housing wires is expected to bring consolidation and some reallocation between the unorganised and organised segments.
B2C to B2B mix has stayed at about 75:25 to 70:30, and management does not expect a meaningful shift.

qa_highlights.question: Had cables and wires volumes declined despite the 14% value growth, and was this destocking or weak end-demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 6% YoY. Industrial cables grew much faster than domestic wires, which were flat. Wires saw destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base from Q4 FY25 channel stocking.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins spike to 37% when revenue was flat, and does the margin normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the spike to year-end releases of dealer incentives and adjustments. The long-term average is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Lloyd channel inventory and sell-in/sell-out trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The first half of April was slow, and some channel inventory built up. Management expects normalised channel inventory by the end of April as summer picks up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue outlook, including a double-digit volume and price-led value growth scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, saying it is difficult to predict amid the war and inflation. It said price hikes could affect demand if they are too steep.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes fully offset raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is striving to pass on costs but must also compete and retain market share, so it will be a balancing act.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken for Lloyd and what more is needed to restore double-digit contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a work in progress. Price increases of 8-15% depending on the AC type are being passed on, with post-war cost increases now flowing through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weighted average price increase above 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said price increases range from 5% to 20% across product ranges, and it did not confirm a weighted average.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 48% growth in the Other segment, and will margins keep expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the Other growth came from solar, which benefited from capacity additions and tight supply. Management expects growth and margin improvement to continue but gave no target.

qa_highlights.question: How much cables and wires price increase was taken, and what was the volume-price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed 6% volume growth and 14% value growth, implying a blended price increase of about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: How will fixed costs and capex change in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some investment will continue across segments in a balanced way. The company aims for revenue growth to outpace expense growth, except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.

risks_watch: Demand elasticity: steep price hikes across categories could slow consumer offtake, and management said it is tracking this closely.
Raw-material and forex inflation from the West Asia conflict, plus gas-supply disruptions that hit production, with only partial pass-through so far.
Lloyd returns: about Rs 4,000 crore of capital is deployed with barely any profitability, and management's turnaround depends on brand building and operating leverage.
Switchgear margin recovery toward 38% depends on price catch-up without losing share.
New entrants in housing wires, including a large cement company, could add pricing pressure.
Fans and cooling Q1 FY27 volumes, which depend on the summer and monsoon, after BEE-norm stocking in Q3 FY26.
Cables and wires margins may have been boosted by one-off inventory gains and year-end adjustments, so the quarter's margin is not a run rate.

It was more confident on the long-term plan (brand, innovation, distribution, medium-term margin improvement of over 2 points) and on the cables and solar growth runways.

517354|2026-06.headline: Havells Q1 FY27: strong revenue growth on calibrated price hikes (7-8% average), but profitability hit by front-loaded A&P; contribution margin stable near 18.3%.
517354|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong revenue quarter with resilient demand despite raw material inflation and West Asia uncertainty. Calibrated, staggered price hikes averaging about 7-8% (range 5-20%) were taken across categories, with cables and wires seeing the largest increases. A&P spend more than doubled year-on-year, which management said front-loaded investment and weighed on quarterly profitability. Renewables is now reported as a separate segment and is growing rapidly, while switchgear sales fell about 4% YoY with margin erosion of around 260 bps. Management gave no formal FY27 guidance, but said the quarter start was positive.

financial_highlights.value: Strong (exact figure not stated in call)

Value growth higher due to price hikes

segments.commentary: AC volume growth in single digits; value growth higher on calibrated price hikes. Management sees Lloyd contribution margin returning to double digits in full (non-seasonal) quarters, versus high single digits recently.

segments.commentary: Sales down ~4% YoY and margin down ~260 bps per analyst; international is ~15% of switchgear sales and was hit by lack of vessels. Management expects international and overall growth to rebound in Q2.

segments.commentary: Volumes flat across wires and cables. Management attributed weakness to distribution shift to sell-out, raw material volatility and heavy A&P spend; cable capacity expansion is under way with ~INR800 crore of FY27 capex.

segments.commentary: Growing rapidly with robust revenue growth; margins held reasonably per management, mainly dragged by panel mix (lower margin than inverters). Solar pumps not yet significant; strategy extends to residential, C&I, BESS and EV chargers. Goldi investment treated as strategic insourcing.

Switchgear domestic demand stable; trade confusion from raw material volatility noted. Management says ~15% international mix.
Management denied any market share loss in ACs or wires, but did not provide share data; said channel inventory was lower than normal at quarter end for cables and ACs.

qa_highlights.question: Has top line lagged industry in Lloyd, ECD and cables because of sharper price hikes, and what is the right volume-price mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the most volatile quarter; calibrated hikes were taken with an eye on market share and channel inventory was kept lean. It believes market share was held or gained on a secondary-sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year A&P budget and is it a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated roughly INR700-800 crore for FY27 (agreed to the 'somewhere around that number' framing). Long-term A&P is about 2.7% of revenue and will remain consistent over 4-5 years; Lloyd A&P elevated for a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is contribution margin going to recover to double digits in Lloyd and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Lloyd should return to double-digit contribution margin in full quarters, not in seasonally weak Q2/Q3. Normalised contribution margin for switchgear was described as roughly 37-40%, and company contribution margin is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the switchgear business weaker in demand and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed West Asia shipping disruption, raw material volatility that hurt pass-through, and trade confusion; domestic demand is stable and recovery expected from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why are cable volumes flat despite capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to raw material volatility slowing sell-in, dealers selling from their own stock as copper prices fell, and a shift to sell-out distribution; it said not to judge on one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will you give FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said Havells does not give annual guidance but the quarter start was positive and it expects resilient growth in volumes and profitability this year.

517354|2026-09.headline: Havells Q2 FY27 revenue grew 35% YoY and EBITDA ~30%, but cables contribution margin fell on aluminium deflation against a high base.
517354|2026-09.overview: Management said all categories grew in Q2 FY27, with revenue up 35% YoY and EBITDA up roughly 30% on operating leverage. PBT growth was moderate because the prior year included a one-time other-income gain. Cables and wires contribution margin declined YoY, while H1 cables margin was about 15%, in line with the long-term average. Lloyd grew revenue 28.5% but margins stayed subdued from raw-material inflation and off-season under-absorption. Calibrated price hikes were taken across categories, and further 5-7% hikes were flagged for Q2/Q3.

517385|2026-03.headline: Symphony FY26 consol revenue fell 28% to ₹1,131 crores; Australia fully impaired, taking PAT to negative ₹141 crores.
517385|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 28% YoY to ₹1,131 crores and PBT before exceptional items fell to ₹149 crores from ₹326 crores, with PAT at negative ₹141 crores after a ₹259 crores consolidated impairment. Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹338 crores (vs ₹488 crores) and EBITDA margin fell to 15.5% from 21.2%, while gross margin held at 46.4%. Management completed a balance-sheet reset: the entire ₹348 crores Australia equity investment is impaired, no further capital will go to Australia, and the US business and Bonaire IPRs were bought into Symphony India for about ₹52 crores. Standalone Q4 revenue was ₹199 crores (vs ₹368 crores) on a high base and channel caution, with management pointing to a possible 4 to 6 week summer runway from mid-May.

517385|2026-06.headline: Symphony Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 8% to ₹378 crore; adjusted PAT up 23% to ₹43 crore, with management warning of near-term margin pressure from input costs.
517385|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹378 crore and EBITDA reported was ₹48 crore (up 26%), but management said June 2026 included a ₹5 crore one-time non-cash charge while June 2025 had ₹9 crore of exceptional income; on that basis EBITDA was ₹53 crore vs ₹38 crore and PAT ₹43 crore vs ₹35 crore. Domestic India revenue grew 15% and modern trade grew over 100%, which management attributed largely to general trade channel inventory being cleared last year. Gross margin was 49.8% and EBITDA margin 12.6%, but management guided to short-term margin pressure from elevated commodity and plastic costs, with only partial price pass-through. Australia (CTPL) remains weak, with management committing to no further capital deployment.

segments.name: IMPCO Mexico
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹54 crore vs ₹66 crore; EBITDA ₹3 crore vs ₹7 crore; PAT ₹1 crore. Management cited two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026).

segments.commentary: Revenue ₹34 crore vs ₹24 crore (up 43%); EBITDA ₹6 crore vs ₹2 crore; PAT ₹5 crore. Standalone entity now debt-free after repaying debt and interest to Symphony India.

segments.commentary: Consol TTM sales about ₹560 crore (~48% of consol revenue); standalone TTM ₹179 crore (~23%), with EBITDA near double-digit margin. Mix includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans, water heaters and exports.

guidance_outlook: Management expects short-term margin pressure from elevated input costs (plastic, commodities); quantum not quantifiable yet and depends on how long the war lasts.
Price hikes of 7% to 10% taken outside household coolers; no hike yet in household cooler segment; further hikes planned but extent uncertain.
Management expects Mexico and USA sales to grow significantly in summer 2027 if summer is normal or robust; no numeric target given.
Bonaire USA and GSK China expected to perform well in the current quarter (Q2 FY27), then more muted; Bonaire USA little revenue in the following two quarters.
No inventory overhang at trade or company level as of June 30, 2026; primary off-season buying by channel partners expected in current and subsequent quarters.
capex_capacity: No further capital allocation to CTPL Australia; management said Australia turnaround to be done without deploying additional capital.
Interim dividend of ₹1 per share (face value ₹2) declared for the quarter, total payout about ₹7 crore.
Impairment and write-off at CTPL Australia recorded in FY26; management said it is behind the company.
GSK China and Bonaire USA sell through company-owned or retail warehouses in the US; no new capacity commissioning details given.
demand_pricing: India revenue grew 15% despite pre-summer channel inventory overhang; modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats) grew over 100%, and modern trade is over one-third of India revenue, with profitability close to general trade.
General trade carried elevated channel inventory from the prior year, which depressed company sales to them; management does not expect 100% modern trade growth to continue.
Standalone exports from India declined due to geopolitical and shipping disruptions; Middle East remains affected and buyer sentiment muted by higher landed costs.
Q1 demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather; no secondary sales expected in the coming quarter, only primary off-season buying.
Coolers in the US are used outdoors and as whole-house or window-mounted units, sold through Home Depot and Lowe's; management said US and Mexico sales were helped by a hot Southwest summer.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales comes from modern trade and e-commerce, and how does its profitability compare with general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose the exact share for competitive reasons. Modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats and regional stores) is over one-third of India top line, with general trade at 60-65%. Modern trade profitability is almost comparable to general trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will input cost inflation such as plastic hit margins in coming quarters, or will it all be passed on given low channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pressure is expected in the short term because costs remain elevated and depend on how long the war lasts. Symphony will pass on some but not all of the increase; the impact is hard to quantify yet despite value engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the modern trade growth above 100%: share gain, market growth, strategy change, or low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the absence of channel inventory in modern trade and e-commerce, versus general trade which carried elevated inventory from the prior year. Management said growth of this scale is unlikely to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What SKUs are driving Bonaire USA growth, and how does its distribution differ from Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: Products are rebranded Indian SKUs, led by the Air Force model, sold to Home Depot and Lowe's, aided by a hot Southwest US summer. Bonaire uses a US warehouse and retailer model, whereas Australia sells mostly to installation companies, with retail still small.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give revenue, EBITDA and PAT for all subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA revenue Rs36 crore (vs Rs27 crore), EBITDA Rs18 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs17 crore. IMPCO Mexico revenue Rs54 crore (vs Rs66 crore), EBITDA Rs3 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs1 crore. GSK China revenue Rs34 crore (vs Rs24 crore), EBITDA Rs6 crore (vs Rs2 crore), PAT Rs5 crore. CTPL Australia revenue Rs27 crore (vs Rs31 crore), EBITDA negative Rs4 crore, reported PAT Rs36 crore including about Rs42 crore one-time gain that is excluded at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken and what is planned, given raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No price hike yet in the household cooler segment. Outside household coolers, 7% to 10% hikes have been taken, with more planned in coming days; the extent depends on when the war ends and costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy to turn around CTPL Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: No additional capital will be deployed; the impairment and write-off is treated as history from FY26. Management said there is nothing new on product, distribution or manufacturing beyond what is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BISP product categories beyond exports, and are tabletop fans and water heaters sold online or offline?
qa_highlights.answer: BISP includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans (sold year-round), water heaters and exports. Management said these are already in modern retail and GT in top cities, but not yet nationwide. BISP is about 48% of consol revenue and 23% of standalone TTM revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there demand for air coolers in the US, a developed market with high per-capita income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coolers are not seen as a poor man's AC outside India and are sold in the US, Europe and the Middle East. In the US they are used outdoors, as whole-house or window-mounted units in the dry Southwest, and their key advantage is portability and plug-and-play use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Mexico and USA sales, given the summer conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico had two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026), so management expects significant growth in summer 2027 if conditions are normal or robust, without giving a number. USA sales should also rise next summer if the summer is similarly good.

qa_highlights.question: Have export shipments resumed, and are geopolitical issues affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The Middle East remains affected. Higher costs elsewhere have made buyers more cautious, since landed costs rose and they cannot pass on the full increase, so purchases are muted and not yet back to normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary outlook for the next few quarters, and what are secondary sales trends in July and early August?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA and GSK China should be fairly good in Q2 FY27 and more muted after that, with Bonaire seeing little revenue in the next two quarters. Q1 was patchy in North and East India. No secondary sales are expected in the coming quarter; only primary off-season buying by channel partners in the current and subsequent quarters.

risks_watch: Short-term gross and EBITDA margin pressure from elevated plastic and commodity costs, with only partial price pass-through; quantum not yet quantified and tied to how long the war lasts.
Price hikes outside household coolers (7% to 10%) are in place, but household cooler pricing is not yet taken; further hikes are uncertain.
Modern trade growth above 100% is driven by the absence of channel inventory and is not expected to repeat; general trade growth is needed to sustain volumes.
Middle East exports remain disrupted and buyer sentiment is muted by higher landed costs; the export recovery timeline is unclear.
CTPL Australia revenue continues to soften; the turnaround is to be achieved without additional capital, with no quantified target.

Weather dependence: Mexico and US sales depend on a robust summer 2027, and North and East India demand was patchy in Q1; Bonaire USA is expected to have little revenue in the two quarters after Q2 FY27.

517385|2026-09.headline: Symphony Q2 FY27 consol revenue rose 31% to ₹275 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to ₹36 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13% vs 6.4%.
517385|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to ₹275 crore and EBITDA rose to ₹36 crore from ₹13 crore, despite gross margin falling about 4%. Standalone revenue rose to ₹170 crore from ₹155 crore, with standalone EBITDA of ₹30 crore vs ₹27 crore, while standalone gross margin fell about 2.3%. Management said Beyond India Summer Products (BISP) now make up 51% of consolidated top line, with a high-single-digit EBITDA margin. The company announced a second interim dividend of ₹2 per share, taking FY27 interim payouts to ₹3 per share (about ₹21 crore so far), and said it will enter room air conditioners, BLDC ceiling fans and air purifiers on an asset-light, outsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: How big could the new categories become, and what are the internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no number. It said it is taking baby steps and will grow cautiously so the categories stay EBITDA accretive, with no delusions of being a top player.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter low-margin RAC when top players struggle with margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rivals have captive manufacturing, while Symphony's model is purely variable cost with no fixed investment. Trade channel year-round engagement is expected to spill over to coolers.

qa_highlights.question: What are channel and company inventory levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said channel normalisation is largely complete. Company inventory was minimal at end-June. Current channel stock is fresh inventory for summer 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected working capital need for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model is low working capital. Products will be bought and sold on demand with no large inventory build, so ROCE should be good.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing for residential ACs and cannibalisation risk for coolers?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-premium pricing with higher specs, comparable to Voltas or Samsung on like-for-like features. Management sees no cannibalisation and expects channel expansion to help coolers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is D2C and how much does the USA/Mexico/Australia business contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give channel-wise splits for D2C; it says D2C has been PAT positive since its second year. IMPCO Mexico ₹40 crore, GSK China ₹23 crore, Australia and USA together ₹46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected in FY27 on a blended basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended margin for FY27 should be higher than the 13-15% range suggested by the analyst, since coolers still dominate sales. It said H2 standalone EBITDA margin should be somewhat above H1's 14.4%.

517498|2026-03.headline: Websol FY26 revenue rose 82% to INR 1,049 crore and PAT 96% to INR 303 crore, with Q4 revenue of INR 401 crore and a INR 1,161 crore order book.
517498|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR 1,049 crore (up ~82%), EBITDA of INR 429 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR 303 crore (28.6% margin), with Q4 the best quarter on most parameters. The company turned net cash surplus, cash from operations was INR 255 crore, and cell capacity doubled to ~1.2 GW after cell line 2 commissioning in September 2025. Management plans to upgrade one 600 MW Mono PERC line to TOPCon (capacity to 1.35 GW) by February 2027, while Andhra Pradesh expansion timing remains undisclosed beyond a June 2027 target. Margin compression was attributed to a higher module mix, silver costs and softer cell and module realisations.

segments.name: Cells (DCR)
segments.commentary: Combined cell utilisation above 90% in FY26; cell realisation ~13-13.5 cents/Wp, softening with silver cost increases. Cells supplied to module makers and captive use in the company's own module line.

segments.name: Modules (DCR)
segments.commentary: Highest-ever module sales in Q4; module realisation ~22-22.5 cents/Wp. Module line (550 MW, Mono PERC) hit a record monthly utilisation of 80%. Module margins are structurally lower than cell margins and drove most of the EBITDA margin dip.

guidance_outlook: TOPCon upgrade of one 600 MW Mono PERC line to ~750 MW (+150 MW), commercial start targeted February 2027, ~2 months ramp to full utilisation; capex INR 250-270 crore; ~15 days revenue loss for that line.
Management expects to approach full run-rate utilisation across all lines in the coming quarter (Q1 FY27).
Andhra Pradesh expansion (2 GW integrated cell and module phase) targeted for June 2027 per management; details to be announced later, no postponement planned.
Ingot and wafer backward integration, with MOU signed with Linton, targeted to commission ahead of ALMM List-3 deadline of June 2028.
Cell and module margins expected to remain healthy over the next 2-3 years with some variability, per management.
capex_capacity: Cell capacity doubled from 600 MW to ~1.2 GW with cell line 2 commissioned in September 2025, funded entirely from internal accruals.
Mono PERC to TOPCon upgrade takes cell capacity to ~1.35 GW; target cell efficiency above 24.5% (vs ~23.3% for PERC); cell size moving from 182x182 to G12R (182x210).
Integrated 4 GW cell and module plan in phases of 2 GW each; the second 2 GW tranche expected around mid-CY28 on TOPCon, with space reserved for future back-contact upgrade.
Module capacity is 550 MW; cell capacity exceeds module capacity, so about 600-750 MW of cell output is sold to third-party module makers.
Management says there is little scope for further expansion at the existing Falta site.
demand_pricing: Focus is on DCR market, mainly PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar; management reports no demand issues and says its entire line is ALMM-listed and DCR-compliant.
Order book is largely module (60%) and mostly sold through solar pump and module players; the company does not tender directly for government orders.
Current TOPCon DCR cell price ~14 cents/Wp; cell realisation 13-13.5 cents/Wp and module 22-22.5 cents/Wp, described as a softening.
Management says it is seeing more orders than the reported INR 1,161 crore but did not quantify further bookings.
Q4 off-take recovered after Q3 delays that were attributed to temporary customer liquidity stress rather than cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to repay the IREDA loan and release pledged promoter shares?

517498|2026-06.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
517498|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to module-heavy mix plus lower cell prices and higher silver/BOM costs; it expects cell margins to fall but not aggressively and to hold current levels for a year or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory rising, and what were Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 7% QoQ, which management attributed to monsoon-led offtake slowdown and cell cost blocked in modules; Q1 realisations were about USD0.125/Wp for cells and INR20.50/W for modules.

qa_highlights.question: What returns does the TOPCon upgrade generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company targeting a larger order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book reports only firm purchase orders and repeat business, and the company is not targeting a higher order book; it sees regular DCR-market inquiries.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TOPCon conversion will serve as practical training before the greenfield expansion; it cited the mono PERC installation timeline as precedent.

517506|2026-03.headline: TTK Prestige Q4 FY26 domestic revenue grew 14.4% and company revenue 12.5%, with operating EBITDA of INR81.7 crore, up 43.8%.
517506|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was driven by domestic demand, with induction cooktops giving a short-term boost to appliances, and exports constrained by supply chain disruption. Operating EBITDA rose 43.8% to INR81.7 crore and PBT rose 35.9% to INR71.9 crore, though exceptional charges relating to the new Labour Code were incurred. Gross margin expanded despite commodity inflation, which management attributed mainly to inventory management and mix, with the mid-quarter price hike only partly visible. For FY26, company revenue grew 9.6% (domestic 9.8%), operating EBITDA grew 12% and PAT rose about 14% to INR185 crore. Management flagged input cost inflation of about 10% post the West Asia conflict and expects margins to dip during the ongoing investment phase.

Cookers industry mix is about 50-55% stainless steel versus about 45% aluminium. Kitchenware plants run at 85%+ utilisation.

segments.commentary: Appliances grew about 10% in FY26 per management, with Q4 lifted by induction cooktop demand driven by a replacement shift during the volatile quarter. Appliance plants run at about 75-80% utilisation; the partner-manufactured model is treated as hybrid in-sourcing.

segments.commentary: Exports were a drag in Q4 due to disrupted global supply chains, despite order inflow. Management says the business is maintained, prior growth was 20-22% on a small base, and the domestic market is the priority.

qa_highlights.question: How much of appliance growth of about 20% is from induction cooktops, and will momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify the induction contribution but said appliances grew reasonably even excluding it. Some trend continues into Q1, and induction adoption may last a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the input cost inflation currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Average input cost increase of about 10%, with some areas up about 15%, post the war scenario. Price hikes are inevitable, weighed against demand.

qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore over 3 years started Q4 FY25, to continue for a few more quarters and taking forms beyond consultants. Management did not give a split for FY26 or FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is general trade growth a trend or new this quarter, and is competition hurting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: General trade growth is attributed to company-specific initiatives on distribution and hygiene. Management said new entrants compete on price and D2C, but the category is growing enough to absorb it; Judge is played separately in the mass segment, and its margins were not compared.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide FY27 ad budget and FY26 amount, saying normally 5-6% of sales is spent on advertising, sales and promotion.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a dip in EBITDA margin during the investment phase lasting about 2 more years, then a return to the earlier 13-14% margin as investments yield results.

qa_highlights.question: Did GST-related channel filling shift growth from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said channel inventory is normalised and GST had little impact on Q4 performance.

517522|2026-03.headline: Rajratan Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin dipped on a ~INR10,000/ton steel price spike it could not pass on; FY26 sales volume up 18% to over 133,000 tons.

517536|2026-09.headline: Onward Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR170.2 crore (+22.4% YoY), EBITDA margin 15.6%, and FY27 guidance was raised to 15-18% growth.

Margin gains were helped by an INR2.9 crore UK R&D credit relating to FY26, which management booked in Q2 after approval in September. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15-18% and EBITDA margin guidance to 13.8-14.3%, replacing the earlier "double-digit" language. Receivable days stretched to about 80, which management attributed to fast growth and customer approval delays.

517544|2026-03.headline: Centum's standalone FY26 revenue rose 25% to a record INR 973 crores, while overseas exits drove a INR 203 crore exceptional charge.

Operating profit targeted to grow 3-4 points above the top line; PAT growth guided at about 3-4 points above top-line growth, and ROE and ROCE expected to return to about 19-20% and 23-24% after Sanand completes.

Sanand Phase 2 EHV and HT cable commercial production is planned by end-March 2027. Sanand sales are targeted at INR 150-200 crores per month in Q3 FY27 and INR 250-300 crores per month in Q3 FY28 (per management); peak Sanand revenue is expected in FY28-29.

Inventory days (about 90 days of COGS) expected to normalise by March 2027. Capex guided at about INR 600 crores a year for 3-4 years, including maintenance capex of INR 100-150 crores (management also cited INR 100-250 crores).
capex_capacity: Total metal-consuming capacity is about 1,83,000 metric tonnes per annum (copper and aluminium). Utilisation in H1 FY27 was 77% in cables, 64% in house wires, 91% in stainless steel wire and 43% in communication cables.
Cumulative capex on Sanand through 30 September 2026 is INR 1,876 crores, with INR 333 crores spent in H1 and about INR 200 crores more expected in H2 FY27. Total H1 capex was INR 402 crores.
CWIP is about INR 1,300 crores as of September, driven mainly by Sanand, and is expected to be capitalised once Phase 2 EHV and HT cable starts by March 2027.
Management expects Sanand EHV ramp-up to take about three months after commissioning for approvals, with sales from the Sanand plant building from the September 2027 quarter.

A new Salarpur project has started and is expected to take about two years to complete. Capex of about INR 600 crores a year is planned for 3-4 years, including growth/infill capex of INR 450-500 crores.
demand_pricing: Export order book is about INR 991 crores, of which roughly 50% is from the USA, with the balance from the Middle East and Australia. Management said the order book converts within 3-4 months.
Order book at the end of September: wire and cable INR 4,927 crores and EPC INR 258 crores.

Pricing is passed through by quoting institutional orders at the prevailing metal price, with a natural hedge from 3-4 months of institutional order book and 3-3.5 months of inventory. Retail prices are revised twice a month.
Management said raw-material price moves pass through and have no effect on margin. It said copper at about 14,800 does not change its volume view, and that volume grows 18-20% if copper stays flat.
Management attributed Q1 vs Q2 margin differences to inventory valuation effects, and said H1 is the right basis for comparison.
Active dealers were 2,146 as of 30 September, against about 2,340 a year earlier. Management said it added more than 25,000 retailers and more than 2 lakh electricians.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 gross margin decline YoY by about 100 bp beyond the EPC loss effect, given prior guidance of margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margin was unrepresentative because of inventory valuation, with the effects averaging out over H1, and that the 11% EBITDA guidance is on an annualised basis. It said H1 operating margin was 11.09% against 10.27-11% over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% margin guidance a cut from the earlier 11-12% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no cut: 11% is the FY27 level, moving to 11-11.5% and then 11.5-12% as Sanand ramps up, with the 11-12% range completing across FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 revenue growth stronger than the usual 20-25% range, and does this imply a slower H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it guides to 25%-plus conservatively to avoid missing guidance. It said H1 growth of about 30-31% already exceeds that guidance, and that the company will add more growth where capital allows.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports and the US order book support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export sales were flat at INR 493 crores (vs INR 472 crores), and the export order book is INR 991 crores with the USA at about 50%. It expects export growth to pick up in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in inventory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than INR 600-700 crores of the inventory build is at Sanand, with the balance from copper valuation at the existing plants. It expects inventory to normalise to about 90 days of COGS by March 2027, and said debtor days have already fallen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EHV revenue opportunity after Sanand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sanand adds INR 1,500-1,700 crores of new EHV capacity in value terms on top of existing EHV sales of about INR 700 crores, with peak Sanand revenue in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is volume versus value, and what is the capital constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided in value terms because budgets are set in value and working capital limits growth to about 25-30%. It said a 16-17% volume growth with 50% price growth would imply a 67-70% value increase, which it considers unfeasible.

Working capital and cash flow: inventory build of about INR 1,200 crores in H1 and the working capital ramp-up at Sanand, with normalisation expected only by March 2027.
Sanand ramp-up pace: Q3 FY27 monthly sales of INR 250-300 crores (per management) and peak utilisation targeted for FY28-29.
Competition from new entrants (including Ultravolt), which management says will not trigger pricing wars, and its impact on dealer and institutional share.
Export order conversion and geopolitical exposure: the order book has a 3-4 month life, and management said export growth depends on geopolitics and competition.
Copper price moves above 15,000 and their effect on demand, and the EPC closure's impact on PAT (about INR 5-7 crores per quarter loss for one or two more quarters).

519003|2026-03.headline: Modi Naturals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% to INR243 crore and PAT 141% to INR19.7 crore, with FY26 PAT up 62.1% to INR50.3 crore.
519003|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR243 crore, EBITDA rose 51.8% to INR24.5 crore (10.1% margin) and PAT rose 141% to INR19.7 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 8.5% to INR719 crore, EBITDA grew 31.2% to INR73.5 crore (10.2% margin, excluding exceptional item) and PAT grew 62.1% to INR50.3 crore. Management said the expanded ethanol plant (282 KLPD, up from 130 KL) started commercial operations late in the year, so its contribution was limited in FY26 and is expected to build from FY27. Growth in the consumer and bulk businesses was mixed, with the consumer segment flat for the year and the bulk segment up sharply.

financial_highlights.metric: Insurance claim received in Q4 FY26 (business interruption, FY24 ethanol breakdown)

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR100 crore (vs INR56.1 crore) and EBITDA INR2.7 crore (vs INR0.9 lakh); FY26 revenue INR198.3 crore (vs INR158.6 crore) and EBITDA INR2.6 crore (vs INR1.7 crore). One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit was shut for non-viability.

segments.name: Ethanol division
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR92.2 crore and EBITDA INR18.5 crore (about 18.8% margin, including an exceptional item); FY26 revenue INR337.4 crore and EBITDA INR58.2 crore (about 17% margin). Management guides about INR950 crore average revenue for FY27 and a sustainable 12-15% EBITDA margin.

Medium-term ambition for the FMCG business of INR500 crore: about INR300-350 crore from oils and INR150 crore from food.
No large capex planned for FY27 beyond up to INR20 crore for a by-product value-addition project in ethanol.

Ethanol order from PSU OMCs in cycle one of ESY 2025-26 (till 31 October 2026) is 47.9 crore litres (47.9 kilo KL as stated), about 150 KLPD at 330 operating days; management said it chose not to bid for private OMC tenders earlier because the plant was not ready.

qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol risk is overcapacity and underutilisation, which management said it is well placed to handle given expansion and tailwinds such as higher blending. Consumer risk is purely execution, given brands and new product lineups.

qa_highlights.question: Is an acquisition in the food sector close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a few food-sector opportunities were evaluated but nothing is firmed up yet; it will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will ethanol value-addition revenue show up by end FY27 or early FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one by-product value-added innovation is already helping EBITDA margins and a second is underway, to be completed in a few months; alcohol-side options include potable (RS/ENA, bottling) and downstream chemicals, with little detail shared.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company of using 282 KLPD, and how long does the PSU OMC order run?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited headroom in consumption and plant location, and said the order covers the ongoing ESY cycle one only, to 31 October 2026, with private OMC registration and tenders expected to add volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol EBITDA margin rise to about 17% from 13% when revenue guidance is INR950 crore, and what is sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the consumer division?

qa_highlights.question: Why does the segment EBITDA differ from the P&L EBITDA?

519126|2026-03.headline: HFL posted record FY26 PAT of INR149 crores (+29% YoY) and guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, while cash flow lagged on working capital.
519126|2026-03.overview: Hindustan Foods delivered record FY26 profitability: total income rose 17% to INR4,264 crores, EBITDA 20% to INR377 crores, and PAT 29% to INR149 crores. Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR104 crores (+28%), and PAT INR41.5 crores (+32%). Footwear was hit hardest by petrochemical and freight inflation in Q4 and expected to remain affected in Q1 FY27, while pass-through in other verticals continues. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores but moved the GST inversion-driven shift from gross to net revenue recognition to Q2-Q3 FY27, and withheld sales and segment profitability guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items Q4 FY26

Broke even in Q2 FY26 and said it is PAT positive, but Q4 margins were hit as polymer prices rose ~50-60% and freight rose; pass-through to customers is delayed and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in Q4 aided by season and new capacity. Panipat plant commissioned April 2026 (capacity ~20,000 tons vs ~35,000-40,000 tons made in FY26). Cone facility acquired and stick facility commissioned; INR50 crore brownfield expansion planned at Lucknow and Panipat.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in the season. New bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27; targets becoming largest independent bottler in India by end FY27, operating as shared manufacturing. INR50 crore investment signed for FY27.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care
segments.commentary: Steady momentum in FY26. Aurangabad personal care facility integrated from 1 April 2026. Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27. INR50 crore HPC investment signed for FY27. Management cites strong engagement in home care.

segments.commentary: Added customers and completed several domestic and international audits; signed 3-4 new customers for the inherited facility (Baddi, acquired from Reckitt, ~INR220 crore difference between paid and book value). Establishing dedicated ayurvedic wellness facility at Baddi. No revenue or profit figures disclosed.

Target of 20% EBITDA growth and 20% ROE mandated for each of the five verticals.

Gross-to-net revenue recognition shift for some food businesses moved from Q1-Q2 to Q2-Q3 FY27; management says no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT, but margins will look better.

Management says EBITDA margin of 10% is achievable; PAT margin of 10% unlikely on a like-to-like basis.

Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27; new beverage bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27.
Baddi ayurvedic wellness facility under establishment, alongside modernisation at the existing Baddi facility; footwear capacity expansion across North and South India.
Management says underutilised assets of about INR508 crores are ramping up; ROCE threshold for new projects is about 18% IRR.
demand_pricing: Footwear polymer prices up roughly 50-60% and freight up; footwear is the only division where raw material pass-through is not immediate. Customers are reportedly supportive.
Most other businesses pass through raw material and packaging cost increases immediately.
Management sees strong customer engagement in home care, beverages and ice cream; export push for healthcare planned, with US modern trade talks under way.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear FY26 sales and profitability, and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales reached about INR500 crores in FY26 and expects INR700-800 crores in FY27. It declined to give a profitability target, citing raw material volatility and ongoing customer talks. CFO said the division broke even in Q2 and is now PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block split between dedicated and shared facilities after completing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Samdani said the split is about 61% dedicated and 39% shared currently and will stay in a similar range on INR2,150 crores of planned gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment moves to net revenue model and what is the impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said this is mainly food, where packaging and some raw materials carry higher GST. The timeline slipped to Q2-Q3 FY27. Bottom-line EBITDA and PAT are unaffected, but margins will look better as sales fall.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pressure in footwear not hit FY27 PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification across categories should offset footwear headwinds through more than compensatory growth elsewhere. It remains confident in the PAT guidance but cannot yet see how long the uncertainty will last.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise profitability and shared versus dedicated ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined segment EBITDA, promising disclosure by year end, and shared that the gross block by segment is in the presentation. Shared manufacturing targets higher ROCE than dedicated. Dedicated ROE targets are 16-22% pre-tax. Footwear is 100% shared.

qa_highlights.question: Financing of incremental capex given working capital pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said working capital credit has been secured across product lines and is not constraining capex. Net debt to equity is 0.84x with cash buffer, but management will be more cautious and not go all out on investments.

519126|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
519126|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.name: Healthcare / OTC Pharma
segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed; management said it is too early to signal the lower end and will revisit in a couple of quarters.
Capacity commercialisation of more than INR500 crore expected in FY27 including carry-forward projects.
Management expects footwear to return to profitability in coming months and to pay off in H2 FY27.
Profit growth expected to outpace revenue growth because customers increasingly supply raw and packing material, so only conversion cost is booked as revenue.
Continued 1:1 debt-equity funding for projects; growth to rely on internal accruals with ROCE threshold of 18%.
capex_capacity: FY27 new project commitments of INR340 crore (INR190 crore newly authorised), plus INR150 crore carried forward from FY26.
Breakdown: Food & Beverages INR210 crore; Ice Cream INR80 crore (Panipat); Home & Personal Care INR50 crore (Lucknow).
Silvassa flood disruption from July rains: partially restored, fully operational by end-August; management says it is insured and has no material long-term impact.
Lucknow greenfield facility due for commissioning later in FY27; Silvassa brownfield to start in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline of inquiries about INR1,000 crore, not yet confirmed; policy is to announce capex only after signing.
demand_pricing: Footwear raw material prices rose ~50-60% (polymer, fabric) and freight rose up to 4x; footwear pricing is fixed 6-12 months ahead, so costs could not be passed through in Q1.
Haryana/NCR minimum wage hike of ~30% hit footwear and was described as a local, one-off issue; other contracts have pass-through clauses.
Footwear order book full for Q2 FY27 onward, with new domestic and multinational customer wins and some lapsed customers returning.
HPC demand has improved materially over the last three months per management, with liquid home care volumes growing near double digits.
US personal care order is on hold due to tariff ambiguity and freight; product development, trials and mould investment are complete.
Middle East export discussions (UAE, Saudi Arabia) put on hold; Dr. Scholl portfolio exported to UK, EU, Australia, NZ and Japan.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company negotiate better terms with customers given GST inversion and weakening competition, and is there any asset revaluation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said GST inversion is not the main driver of outsourcing and that the company is better placed to handle it. Assets have not been revalued and the business model does not depend on it; the value sits on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Can footwear raw-material cost increases be built into contracts structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shoe contracts are set 6-8 months ahead with fixed prices, so mid-season changes are not industry practice. Brands have agreed to absorb some cost for the coming season, and pass-through is now being achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the INR340 crore of new projects by segment.
qa_highlights.answer: Food & Beverages INR210 crore across five units, Ice Cream INR80 crore at Panipat, and HPC INR50 crore at Lucknow for a bar and liquid line.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear utilisation and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was poor; utilisation is about 80-90% from August with a full order book and new logos, with the business expected to pay off in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear employee cost share and profit impact of INR210 crore beverage capex at 18% ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Footwear employee cost is about 35-40% of Q1 total. Beverage units are expected online by Dec/Jan on anchor-tenant basis; the analyst's ROCE maths was corrected to EBIT, with 1:1 debt-equity funding implying interest outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block growth outlook over 3-5 years versus sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block will grow faster than sales because customer-supplied raw material means only conversion cost is booked as revenue. It expects to fund growth from internal accruals at 1:1 leverage with an 18% ROCE threshold.

risks_watch: Footwear margin recovery depends on brands absorbing cost and on Middle East-driven material and freight costs easing; ~INR6 crore hit in Q1.
Silvassa restoration by end-August and insurance recovery; watch for any Q2 output shortfall.
Execution of INR500 crore capex this year, and whether Lucknow and Silvassa start on time.
US tariff ambiguity keeps personal care export orders on hold.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation for shared sites; footwear ROCE is below the 18% threshold, per management.
key_quotes: we delivered our highest ever quarterly PAT with a growth of nearly 1/3, 33% over last year.
we are confident that our customers will support us in mitigating the losses incurred due to these causes and that the division will return to profitability in the coming months.
I think it's too early to say that, Virat. We have continued to reaffirm our guidance.
I think the shoe business should finally start paying off in the second half of this financial year.

Cautious and somewhat defensive on footwear: it is described as temporarily stressed, management repeatedly declined to give plant-level utilisation or category EBITDA, and it was reluctant to say GST inversion is a tailwind or to give a hit ratio on the project pipeline.

rows.why: Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa, Lucknow HPC bar and liquid lines due later in FY27, and Class III medical device certification started at Chennai, though no specific launch dates were given beyond these.

rows.label: Footwear return to profitability
rows.why: Utilisation 80-90% from August with full order book from Q2 FY27 and price pass-through from Q1, after ~INR6 crore Q1 cost hit; footwear ROCE still below 18% threshold per management.

rows.label: Silvassa flood disruption resolved
rows.why: Plant partially restored from July rains, management expects full operation by end-August and says it is insured with no material long-term impact.

519183|2026-03.headline: ADF Foods Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR196.7 crore (+23.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.4%, but Middle East (GCC) exposure clouds FY27 guidance.
519183|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to a record INR196.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR34.3 crore (17.4% margin, +190 bps) and PAT of INR25.9 crore (+57.6%). Standalone FY26 revenue grew 10.3% to INR527.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 24.8%. The Surat greenfield plant began commercial production in March 2026, but West Asia disruption stopped GCC shipments in March and April, and management cut its outlook to a conditional range if the disruption persists. Net cash surplus stands at INR78.2 crore and the final dividend is 30% of face value (60% for FY26).

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Management guided Ashoka to grow about 30-35% in FY27; FY26 Ashoka revenue was about INR308 crore per an analyst's calculation that management did not dispute. Core markets are North America (incl. Canada), UK and Europe, with Australia and New Zealand also growing.

segments.name: Truly Indian (mainstream US brand)
segments.commentary: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well. Listed in about 3,000 US stores including Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons and Whole Foods; repeat rotations are seen at some Costco divisions.

segments.name: B2B and private label
segments.commentary: B2B and private label make up about 20% of revenue. Distribution business added new regional brands and Ashoka SKUs (staples, oils, flour), with SKUs rising from about 440 to about 600.

segments.name: GCC / Middle East
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue (described as under 15%). Shipments were nil in March and about 80-85% of GCC business was lost, with only 1-2 ports operating in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore, conditional on West Asia stabilising within about a month; management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues.
If GCC contribution stays at zero, FY27 growth is about 12-15% (roughly INR800-850 crore); with GCC normalised, growth of 30%+ and the INR925-1,000 crore band.
Surat plant expected to contribute INR40-50 crore revenue in FY27; full capacity implies upwards of INR200-250 crore (Phase 2 included), with full utilisation targeted in year 3.
Management expects to maintain high-teen consolidated EBITDA margins; Surat margins at full capacity expected to be similar to existing facilities.
Freight costs up about 3-4% of revenue in March; management said this is expected to ease over about the next two months. Analyst was told to add about 1 percentage point of freight in the base.
PLI incentive expected to be similar in FY27 (about INR16 crore) and is the final year of the scheme.
Capex of INR20-25 crore in FY27 (pizza base line, Surat balance payments), plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking; a further US warehouse is planned around Q3 FY27.
Potential INR30 crore quarterly revenue risk from GCC on a run-rate basis, as an analyst framed it and management confirmed.
capex_capacity: Approximately INR124 crore capex over the last 2 years across Nadiad, Nashik brownfield and Surat greenfield; Surat total investment including Phase 2 is a little above INR100 crore.
Surat Phase 1 (2 product lines) commenced production in the third week of March 2026; Phase 2 adds a product line (pizza base) in Q3 FY27.
Surat utilisation expected at about 35-40% in Phase 1 during FY27; Phase 2 contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27.
Average capacity utilisation across product lines was about 70-75% in FY26.
US warehouse: freezer space above 100% utilised (using outside storage); ambient space about 85% utilised. Another distribution centre planned, probably in Q3 FY27.
Debottlenecking at Nadiad and Nashik (flatbread and snack lines) drove most of the FY26 volume growth.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, with the balance from product mix and rupee depreciation; management said prices were not increased.
Truly Indian initial traction is mainly distribution-led, with some repeats at Costco and other chains; management sees the Indian ethnic category at an inflection point in the US mainstream channel.
No impact seen from GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic) on demand; the whole range is vegetarian and vegan.
GCC shipments were nil in March 2026 because shipping lines were not taking containers. Other markets saw longer transit times and higher freight rates but no loss of sales.
Freight costs rose sharply in March 2026 as vessels were jammed and US routes lengthened; the company shares freight cost with GCC distributors 50:50 on those routes.
Tariff refund: applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million following a Supreme Court directive; nothing received in FY26, and any refund will be accrued in the year received.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 guidance of INR925-1,000 crore reconcile with the growth drivers, given Ashoka and Truly Indian?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR925-1,000 crore band, conditional on the Middle East reopening. Ashoka is expected to grow 30-35% and Truly Indian INR75-80 crore. With zero GCC, growth is 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East (GCC) impact and worst-case scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC is under 15% of revenue. About 80-85% of GCC business has been lost, with nil March shipments. In the zero-GCC case, FY27 growth is about 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Surat plant ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Surat contribution is INR40-50 crore; full capacity implies INR200-250 crore once Phase 2 is complete. Full utilisation is targeted in year 3.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight-cost increase should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rose by about 3-4% of revenue in March. The CFO said about 1 percentage point should be added to the base, with normalisation expected over about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and total Surat spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat total is a little above INR100 crore. FY27 capex is INR20-25 crore (pizza line and balance payments) plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Will PLI incentive continue after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme, expected at a similar level (about INR16 crore). The scheme covered 50% of marketing spend.

risks_watch: West Asia / GCC disruption: about 15% of revenue, with nil March shipments and only 1-2 ports open in April; guidance depends on normalisation within about 1-2 months.
Freight and logistics costs: March spike of about 3-4% of revenue; management expects normalisation but this is unproven.
Loss of PLI incentive after FY27 (about INR16 crore per year) will remove a support to margins.
Surat ramp-up: Phase 2 starts in Q3 FY27 and contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27; execution risk.
Freezer capacity in the US warehouse is above 100%, which requires outside storage and a new distribution centre.

519183|2026-06.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
519183|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of margin). Final year is FY27; management expects brand investment as a % of sales to fall as brands scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see catch-up from Q1 shipment shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some carry-forward is expected in Q2, but it could slip into Q3 if container availability does not improve.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; a carry-forward of unshipped goods could push revenue from Q2 into Q3.
Freight costs and whether pass-through holds in the US, where roughly 75% of freight increase is being passed on.
Tariff: the 10% rate is still applicable, with no certainty on the future rate.
Margin dependence on the one-time tariff refund and on PLI, which ends after FY27.
Surat ramp-up is slow (about 30% utilisation this year), which limits near-term operating leverage.
Soul domestic brand is growing slowly, while brand investments in Truly Indian and Soul continue.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR24 crore a year earlier per analyst

financial_highlights.value: USD2.08 million = INR19.69 crore received; USD0.77 million (~INR7 crore) booked in P&L in Q1

key_quotes: With strong business momentum, we remain well positioned to deliver revenue upwards of INR900 crores in financial year 27 while maintaining healthy high-teen EBITDA margins.
So even in the month of June, we could not ship out 30% of our goods which were ready due to non-availability of the ships and containers.
So, I think it's still continuing at 10% only at the moment. How it goes future is anyone's guess, Saurabh.
So basically, we have lot of structured programs in our manufacturing and supply chain operations.
