519397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year on revenue and profit, with export revenue up about 23% and export volumes up about 8%. Q4 revenue grew about 25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore, but margins were squeezed by the West Asia conflict, which forced rerouting of Middle East-bound shipments, higher logistics costs and inventory build-up, along with sharp fishmeal and soya price increases. US tariffs on Indian shrimp fell from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026, and management is targeting FY27-28 export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore. 519552|2026-09.headline: Heritage Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR13,196 million, with EBITDA margin at 5.6%, up 98 bps QoQ despite milk procurement cost up 11% YoY.
519552|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 19% YoY to INR13,196 million and H1 grew 18% to INR26,577 million. EBITDA was INR740 million (5.6% margin), up 98 bps sequentially, while PAT was INR309 million. Landed milk procurement cost rose 11% YoY to INR47.73/litre, and management passed through about 8% weighted average price increase, with a larger hike taken in September that benefits Q3. Management expects further procurement inflation in Q3 and is watching the post-Diwali buffalo flush.

financial_highlights.change: Margin +98 bps QoQ vs Q1; ~4.6% to 5.6% per management

financial_highlights.metric: VAP share of revenue (ex ghee & butter)
Broader VAP incl. consumer ghee & butter

segments.name: Core milk
segments.commentary: Milk sales volume +2% YoY to 12.35 lakh litres/day in Q2 (H1 +1% to 11.99 lakh L/day). Price up ~6% in Q2, with milk alone taken up ~6%.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Lassi volumes +89%, buttermilk +56%, ice cream +44%, paneer +21%, curd +15% in Q2. Curd daily sales crossed 500 tonnes; Nourish+ paneer >15% of paneer portfolio.

segments.name: Ice cream / Get-A-Way
segments.commentary: New ice cream facility commissioned; Heritage supplies 3,272 litres/day to Get-A-Way (71% stake). Own ice cream revenue expected at INR170-180 crore this year vs ~INR110 crore last year.

segments.name: Heritage Novandie (LIVO yogurt)
segments.commentary: Now wholly owned; management says LIVO is among top 5 yogurt brands in India. No financials given.

segments.name: Heritage Nutrivet (Animal Nutrition)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR853 million (+47%) and PBT INR37 million; H1 revenue INR1,581 million (+42%) and PBT INR56 million. Cattle feed sales up 47% YoY in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Q3 price benefit expected: September price hikes were well above the 8% Q2 weighted average and will accrue in Q3; October opened at higher consumer price levels than Q2.
Management expects procurement prices to rise in Q3 at around 11% YoY, though it hopes for post-Diwali cooling as buffalo flush arrives; no firm view on raw milk direction.
Operating leverage expected to improve in Q3 over Q2, which was better than Q1; depreciation from recently capitalised projects weighing on PBT/PAT.
Value-added product share expected to keep expanding in Q3; first 15 days of Q3 showed continuing trend and ghee volume growth expected to be strong in Q3 on festive timing.
Management indicated a Rs 0.5/litre fall in procurement price would add about 0.7% to bottom line (~INR3 crore per month).
Ice cream target of INR500 crore revenue in 6-7 years from commissioning.

Cow milk procurement inflation outpacing buffalo as producers switch to cow milk; buffalo supply constrained by monsoon/El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Are milk procurement prices moderating in the buffalo flush, given El Nino and broad-based feed/fodder inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices rose in Q2 as in the prior year; regional monsoon performance is uneven (north floods, south drought). Milk procurement volume rose 7% YoY and cattle feed sales rose 47% YoY in Q2. Post-Diwali cooling is hoped for, but October procurement prices are slightly above September.

qa_highlights.question: Did weather help the 32% VAP growth, and how much price was taken in Q2 across milk and VAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 benefited from better weather; Q2 VAP growth was described as broad-based and not weather-driven, with metro rainfall normal or above. Weighted average price increase was about 8% (milk about 6%, VAP 9-10%), staggered over July-September, with September hikes higher than 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 procurement inflation remain near 11% YoY and how do price hikes compare QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 11% YoY procurement increase might continue into Q3 but hoped for buffalo-flush relief. It declined to speculate on raw milk direction and said Q3 consumer price levels are well above Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How are cooperatives (Nandini, Aavin) pricing and what is the pass-through on falling milk prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Aavin raised farm-gate price from INR38 to INR44 (about INR6/litre); Karnataka plans INR8/litre consumer hike from 1 November, with Bangalore sales upside. Management said INR0.5/litre lower procurement cost adds about 0.7% to bottom line (about INR3 crore per month on 1.8 million litres/day).

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on procurement, and what drives EBITDA vs PBT gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the question speculative but said core dairy growth of about 17% was 49 points price and 51 points volume. Depreciation from projects capitalised at start of FY27 is weighing on PBT/PAT, and operating leverage is expected to improve in Q3 over Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach about 7% and what cost heads drove the margin rise from 4.6% to 5.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin moved from 4.6% to 5.6%. Employee costs fell about 1% of revenue, opex about 0.6%, and freight about 0.1%; raw material was the only rising cost line as a share of revenue. No explicit 7% target was given.

risks_watch: Procurement inflation: management expects around 11% YoY procurement increase to continue into Q3, with buffalo supply constrained by El Nino and monsoon deficits in southern states.

Ghee volumes were flat in Q2 and depend on festive timing; Q3 ghee volume growth is unverified beyond the first 15 days.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue grew 19% year -on-year to INR13,196 million in quarter 2, taking H1 revenue to INR26,577 million, up 18%.
So we are exiting Q2 in a much stronger position.
So operating leverage in Q2 is better than Q1. And the operating leverage in Q3 will be better than Q2.
Raw milk prices is speculative, I do not wish to make any comment.
So the more and more value -added product contribution goes up, the better will be our ability to pass on to our consumers as much as raw milk inflation happens.

519600|2026-03.headline: CCL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 46% to INR1,226.39 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR193.76 crore; FY27 guidance is ~15% volume and EBITDA growth.
519600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 46% YoY to INR1,226.39 crore, with EBITDA up 16% to INR193.76 crore and net profit up 12% to INR114.53 crore. Management attributed the top-line surge mainly to green coffee price pass-through under the cost-plus model, with volume growth of about 18-20%. Net debt fell by more than INR750 crore to about INR1,073 crore, and net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.45x from 3.1x. Management guided FY27 volume and EBITDA growth of about 15% each, with no large capex planned for two years.

segments.commentary: Management said B2C EBITDA is around 4-5% and will be held at that level, with surplus reinvested over the next 3-4 years. Quick commerce business is about INR100 crore annually.

segments.commentary: International brand Percol contributes about INR25-30 crore in the UK this year; management targets about INR100 crore within 2-3 years and is evaluating the US and Vietnam.

qa_highlights.question: What was volume growth and was EBITDA per kg down sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 18-20% on a four-quarter view and Q4 was similar. Q4 EBITDA per kg dipped on product mix, but FY26 per-kg EBITDA improved YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin contraction due to coffee prices, and what is the coffee outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA-to-sales decline is optical because of cost-plus pass-through; per-kg EBITDA is unchanged. Coffee prices may soften, which would lower value growth while volume grows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA growth be sustained, and why did FY26 outperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is about 15% EBITDA growth in line with volume. FY26 gains from freeze-dried mix and efficiencies are already in the base and are unlikely to repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capacity for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex planned for two years, only maintenance capex of INR25-35 crore. Growth beyond capacity could come from tie-ups or outside capacity purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost not fall with lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR25-30 crore of interest was capitalised last year for Vietnam; borrowing cost is 7-7.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the export and freight cost effects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of exports are FOB. CIF contracts absorb freight and insurance increases, which cannot always be passed on; availability has not been affected.

Freight, insurance and energy cost pressures on CIF contracts from the Middle East situation.

519600|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.76% to INR1,203.59 crore on ~20% volume growth, with EBITDA up 21.84% to INR196.69 crore and net debt cut to INR963 crore.
519600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 turnover was INR1,203.59 crore (up 13.76% YoY) on roughly 20% volume growth, with coffee price pass-through muting top-line growth. EBITDA rose 21.84% to INR196.69 crore and PAT rose 61.31% to INR116.87 crore. Net debt fell to INR963 crore from INR1,073 crore at March 2026, and management reiterated 15% full-year volume guidance without upgrading it. Management said EBITDA per kg (about INR140, per analyst question) should hold for FY27, and standalone margins were hit by logistics and packaging cost increases.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR1,073 crore at March 2026, about INR100 crore QoQ reduction
term loan INR517 crore, working capital INR751 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore total, of which about INR125 crore branded

segments.name: Coffee B2B (contract manufacturing, cost-plus)
segments.commentary: Volume growth about 20% in Q1 against 15% full-year guidance; revenue growth of 13.76% lagged volume because of lower green coffee prices (INR3,300-3,800 per kg range cited). Capacity utilisation about 65-70% in aggregate, with freeze-dried running higher than spray-dried.

segments.name: Domestic branded B2C
segments.commentary: Gross turnover about INR180 crore, of which about INR125 crore branded, with Q1 growth about 26% YoY. Share claims: above 6% urban share in South India, double-digit share at Reliance and DMart, and very high single digits on quick commerce.

segments.commentary: Percol UK turned around; FY26 top line about INR26-27 crore. Distributor talks under way in the US and Middle East, with some deals expected to close in a couple of months.

segments.commentary: Broader rollout began about 5-6 days before the call, with banana chips added to chegodi and murukku; management expects only a couple of crore of revenue in FY27.

EBITDA per kg to stay around current levels (about INR140) for FY27; EBITDA growth expected to track volume growth.
Domestic branded volume growth of 20-25% in FY27 and branded sales of INR550-600 crore, with margins kept at 5-6% EBITDA rather than harvested.

Volume growth of about 15% sustained for the next 3-4 years, with B2C growing 25-30%.

Parent-company capacity has been flat for more than 10 years; future volume growth will come mainly from subsidiaries.

demand_pricing: Green coffee prices around INR3,300-3,800 per kg; management sees volatility from Brazil supply versus El Nino risk to the Vietnam crop due in Nov-Dec.

Freeze-dried earns about 30-40% more EBITDA than spray-dried, per management's rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Can 15% volume growth continue given coffee volatility and rupee depreciation, and will margins benefit from depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15% volume guidance without upgrading. It said a forex policy covers appreciation, and that EBITDA growth will track volume growth on a cost-plus basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will capacity constrain growth beyond FY28 at 95%+ utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity will not hinder growth. Expansion is considered at 75-85% utilisation, with 9-12 months lead time, and the company is willing to use tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA per kg likely to rise further, and why was Q1 lower historically?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided EBITDA per kg to hold for FY27. It said seasonality is limited and the historical Q1 dip was likely coincidence or mix-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic market share, and when will the branded business turn PAT-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Urban share in South India is above 6%, with double-digit share in Reliance and DMart. Management does not report PAT for the domestic business separately and is keeping EBITDA at 5-6% to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt repayment and cash deployment plans?

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone performance weaker than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to logistics costs, small-pack packaging price increases, and the high base of the prior-year standalone quarter. It said the standalone business is in line with Q4 FY26.

520008|2026-06.headline: Rico Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~39% to INR755 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% and PAT turned to a INR3.4 crore loss.

Profitability was hit by about INR24 crore of higher other operating expenses (including air freight and sorting costs of about INR13 crore), plus an estimated INR10 crore raw-material settlement lag. Management reiterated full-year revenue of about INR3,250 crore and said margins should recover from Q3 as air freight ceases and customer price revisions flow through. Q2 margins are expected to be better than Q1 but still in between the Q1 level and the targeted trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aluminium price assumption behind FY27 guidance?

520057|2026-03.headline: JTEKT India FY26 sales grew 11% vs 9% PV market, but full-year EBITDA margin slipped to 7.5% from 7.6% on mix and forex.
520057|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 11% against passenger vehicle market growth of 9%, helped by GST cuts and new Maruti Suzuki models (e Vitara, Victoris). Second-half EBITDA margin recovered to 8.48% from 7.71%, while H1 margin was 6.3%, leaving the full year at 7.5%. Management attributed the margin drag to product mix (Honda down about 33%, 0.33% impact), a forex accounting effect (0.23%) and US tariffs (0.24%), which it called largely temporary. New capacity (CVJ line 2, MS Gear line 5 and 6, CPS line 3) is still under-utilised, and management expects it to reach full utilisation over 1 to 1.5 years. A Brazil export order from the JTEKT group starts dispatch in May 2026.

Competition in CVJ from GKN-linked and other suppliers, which hold over 60% of Maruti's business; management targets at least 15% CVJ share.
Management said it is not supplying Renault's Duster.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined from 29% to 27% over two years, and how should they trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was 6.3% and H2 8.48%; net variable cost drag of 0.18% came from a 0.33% mix effect (Honda, Renault-Nissan, Toyota down; Maruti GST-driven models higher), 0.23% forex accounting effect and 0.24% US tariffs, offset by export gains and lower warranty. Management called these temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Has Toyota's Bidadi third line commenced, and what is Toyota's revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bidadi line had not commenced per its understanding; a new Maharashtra facility is expected in H1 FY29, lifting Toyota capacity to about 1 lakh vehicles. JTEKT is the only steering supplier to Toyota.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for other driveline products beyond CVJ and hub bearings for JTEKT's group?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan is finalised; management said it needs 1-1.5 years to stabilise CVJ first. It noted export opportunities for CVJ parts to group entities.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the INR 1,000 crore top-line addition by FY27 and whether revenue can double in 3-4 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 300 crore was added in FY26; with 10% market growth and INR 75-100 crore exports, about INR 500 crore more is possible in FY27 (about INR 800 crore total). It declined to share a formal business plan and said growth depends on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 capex and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be lower than the last two years, with about INR 100 crore for Gujarat plus normal capex. ROCE excluding CWIP is above 11%, and full utilisation should push it back toward earlier levels (about 16-17%).

qa_highlights.question: Driveline pipeline, CVJ margins and fixed asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: CVJ margins are better than most MS Gear products and it is 100% localised. Target fixed asset turnover is about 3x overall; CVJ is lower (about 1.5x), CPS 2.5-3x, manual gear 2-2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Potential for exports to US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brazil is the first step, with a Stellantis order, and that a further order could follow once quality and cost are established. No firm US or Europe plan was given.

522113|2026-03.headline: Timken India Q4 FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time, up 14.2% YoY to INR10,731 million; PBT margin 19.3%.

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

risks_watch: Steel and other input cost inflation: about INR5,000 per tonne of steel price increases; pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts that are fixed until renewal.
Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.
Parent's 80/20 review and divestments (belts, automotive OE): the Indian implications are unclear, and management said it will review which assets can be used for growth in India.
Export exposure to geopolitics; Europe, China and ASEAN are down; US tariff status was not confirmed on the call.
Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.
key_quotes: We have delivered high double-digit revenue growth this quarter Y-o-Y, driven by resilient demand, especially in the core segments, and our execution both for export and domestic.
So, the revenues are growing with every passing week, and I will ask Sujit to add more colour to the whole thing so that you get a little bit more specific answer.
So railway is a little bit sluggish as we speak, but it is an issue of time, so it will come back.
It is tough to tell you exactly percentage. Different customers, different behaviour.
522113|2026-06.management_tone: Management sounded confident on Q1 execution, Bharuch ramp-up pace and cost pass-through in heavy-truck and tractor markets. It was cautious and deferred on exact price-recovery percentages, rail timing, US tariff rate and future cost escalation tied to the Middle East conflict and Brent.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and flat QoQ; heavy-truck and off-highway price increases are sticking, offset by unfavourable Q1 mix and fixed-price rail and PSU contracts that reprice only at renewal.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bharuch SRB line is already running at 40-45% utilisation and is targeted at about 70% by Aug-Sep 2026, with CRB ramp toward Q2-end and Q3; Jamshedpur rail capacity is due for commercial production by calendar year-end 2026 (Q3 FY27).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue grew about 15% YoY to INR929 crore, process is up about 28-30% from metals and wind, and Bharuch SRB utilisation is set to rise from 40-45% to about 70%; rail is only about 3% growth and government procurement is slow.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is held at about 8-10% of sales with project work on track, and Bharuch and Jamshedpur capacity are already under construction, so no new capex round was signalled; utilisation at the Bharuch plant is only 40-45%, so no capacity squeeze prompts a fresh announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue grew about 15% YoY to INR929 crore, with process up 28-30% and exports including the US up, but no numeric revenue guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Steel prices rose about INR5,000 per tonne in total, pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts fixed until renewal, and the Bharuch ramp must reach about 70% SRB utilisation by Aug-Sep or margins weigh; gross margin was 39.9%.

rows.label: Steel cost pass-through to heavy-truck and off-highway contracts
rows.why: Steel rose about INR5,000 per tonne in total and management said it will keep passing cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew, with most customers already paying.

rows.label: Parent 80/20 portfolio review and India focus
rows.why: Management said 80/20 is not yet a strategy change for India, but it will review which assets can be used for growth in India, with the belts and automotive OE divestments unclear.

rows.label: NCLT approval of Timken GGB Technology merger
rows.why: The merger is pending NCLT approval per the risks watch list, but no timing was given on the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 execution, Bharuch ramp pace and heavy-truck/tractor price pass-through, and cautious on exact price-recovery percentages, rail timing, US tariff rate and future cost escalation; analysts probed the 80/20 review, rail outlook and cost pass-through.

522113|2026-09.headline: Timken India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 25.4% YoY to INR 969 crore, with PBT up 29.5% to INR 156 crore and PBT margin at 16.1%.
522113|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with standalone revenue of INR 969 crore (up 25.4% YoY and about 4.3% QoQ) and PAT of INR 116 crore (up 29.7% YoY). Margins improved despite higher depreciation from new vessels, fuel and gas costs. The new Bharuch plant is ramping up, with SRB lines at 70% utilisation and CRB lines below 60%, and revenue from the plant at about INR 75 crore. Management flagged rising input costs, a delayed rail tender that has since moved toward orders, and an unfavourable mix that drove a 130 bps gross margin decline QoQ.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 786 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR 156.7 crore in Q2, 16% of revenue; low share as the global rail tender was delayed, which drove the unfavourable mix.

segments.name: Mobile others (automotive)
segments.commentary: INR 204 crore, 21% of revenue.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR 148.8 crore, 15% of revenue.

segments.name: Process industries
segments.commentary: INR 190.9 crore, 20% of revenue; wind cited as doing well, and management expects stable growth ex-CRB/SRB.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR 262.7 crore, 27% of revenue; up about 60% YoY and 30% QoQ per analyst's figures, with export incentives reported separately.

segments.name: Bharuch (CRB/SRB)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR 75 crore in Q2; plant at about 60% average utilisation, SRB lines at 70% and CRB lines below 60%; sales mainly intercompany exports.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 utilisation at Bharuch expected at about 70-75% overall, with CRB at 50-60% and SRB at 70% as of the call.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR 120 crore): trial runs in November-December 2026, followed by PPAP and qualification; commercial production targeted by December.
Railway tender expected to convert to orders within about 3 weeks, with interim wagon-builder orders already placed.
Management expects overall export momentum to be healthy in coming quarters, with rail exports more gradual.
Cost inflation (carbides, steel, gases, labour) expected to continue; management aims to pass it on to customers.
Q3 seasonality expected to soften because of calendar year-end export timing.
Proposed amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited into Timken India is progressing; regulatory process ongoing.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramp-up: lines capitalised; overall utilisation about 60% in Q2, with SRB at 70% and CRB below 60%.
Jamshedpur rail expansion, about INR 120 crore, on target; trial runs Nov-Dec 2026.
Plain bearing investment at Bharuch on target; GGB FRC and metal polymer investments of about INR 35 crore each (INR 70 crore total), approved and underway, with asset turn of about 1.5-2x.
Management said GGB machines are installed at Bharuch but not yet capitalised; imported GGB product currently sold while local production is pending.
New vessels added, raising depreciation.
demand_pricing: Demand described as okay across key end markets; domestic demand seen as robust given GDP growth of about 7% and infrastructure spending.
Rail and heavy truck seen as attractive segments; off-highway behaving well globally and in India.
Price pass-through: management said the industry cannot absorb input cost increases and aims to pass them on; automotive customers may delay pass-through.
Gross margin down about 130 bps QoQ: roughly 50% from unfavourable mix (lower rail and distribution share) and 50% from input cost vs price timing.
Wind: domestic wind market recovering; Timken India sells gearbox bearings and buys main-shaft wind bearings from sister concerns.
India cost competitiveness described as favourable versus global peers, though not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise revenue for Q2 and Bharuch utilisation versus the 70% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Segment split given (Rail 16%, Mobile others 21%, Distribution 15%, Process 20%, Exports 27%). Overall Bharuch utilisation about 60%; SRB at 70%, CRB below 60%; Bharuch revenue about INR 75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the cost increase be passed on, and how much did it impact Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry must pass costs on; automotive will delay. The 130 bps gross margin decline was split about 50/50 between unfavourable mix and input cost timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall and CWIP double?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the drop was an accounting reclassification between other expenses and depreciation of about INR 1.3 crore, not a structural decline.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch margins versus TRB, and the Jamshedpur rail timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are not disclosed at plant level; industrial CRB/SRB directionally better than automotive. Rail expansion trial runs in Nov-Dec, with qualification to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bharuch's utilisation reach 80-85% by year-end, and how does the mix affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 70-75% overall by year-end; margin accretion expected once critical mass is reached, with CFO noting Q3 seasonal softening.

qa_highlights.question: How is wind positioned, and is GGB winning orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Timken India focuses on gearbox bearings, not main-shaft; GGB has not yet capitalised local production but is winning orders via imported product, with local output at Bharuch to follow.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (carbides, steel, gas, fuel, labour) with limited ability to absorb; timing gap in price pass-through.
Automotive customers may delay price pass-through.
Bharuch ramp-up pace: CRB lines below 60% utilisation and reliance on intercompany exports for current sales.
Rail tender conversion into orders and rail mix, which drove the QoQ margin drop.
Depreciation step-up from new vessels and Bharuch; CWIP nearly doubled.
Geopolitical and trade uncertainty affecting global demand and supply chains.
Pending amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology into Timken India.

Management was candid on the Bharuch utilisation gap and on the timing of rail orders, and it deflected precise margin figures (Bharuch margins, cost-competitiveness) by giving directional answers only.
key_quotes: And the momentum is going to be pretty healthy in quarters to come for sure.
Carbides have gone 200% up. Steel is going up and then your gases have already gone up.
So SRB lines, we have already reached 70% for the quarter, what we promised in the last quarter.
That obviously, we don't state. So I will just tell you directionally.

522163|2026-06.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
522163|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR922 crore at 30 Jun 2026; positive INR691 crore post-QIP
INR1,640 crore gross (INR1,614 crore net per Q&A)
INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 (~$445 mn), across 12 product lines
financial_highlights.change: ~2x FY26 revenue; >INR1,000 crore fresh wins since April

financial_highlights.value: Negligible in Q1 due to carried-forward losses; benefit expected for at least two years

segments.name: Medium voltage (11–66 kV) and EHV (132 kV+) cables
segments.commentary: Largest order-book block; management targets moving mix up the voltage curve, with 66 kV and above EBITDA guided at 18–22%. A INR435 crore data center order sits in this band.

segments.name: Low voltage (1.1 kV) cables
segments.commentary: Q1 mix skewed toward LV and conductors because MV/EHV cannot be laid in flood conditions; LV EBITDA guided at 8–9%. New copper LV facility (brownfield, ~42,000 km capacity, revenue potential ~INR1,880 crore) targeted for FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: Conductors (incl. HTLS, AL-59)
segments.commentary: Conductor EBITDA guided at 9–10%. Management says AL-59 is now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped producing ACSR.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the fourth rod mill, the incremental silane line and the CCV line, and sixth CCV line delivery.
qa_highlights.answer: Rod mill by 15 Oct, silane line by 15 Sep, CCV line in March 2027; sixth CCV line to be ordered this month, delivery assurance for August 2027 and commissioning by December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Net worth and use of QIP proceeds.
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth was negative INR922 crore at 30 June 2026 and is positive INR691 crore after the INR1,614 crore net QIP proceeds. Planned use: INR130 crore LV expansion, INR74 crore balancing equipment, INR325 crore general corporate purposes, INR350 crore promoter unsecured loan repayment, with about INR750 crore for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery expectation on the INR957 crore legacy receivables.
qa_highlights.answer: A special team is evaluating recovery; management expects about INR300 crore to be recovered over 12–18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation outlook after the audit qualification was resolved.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 depreciation will be the run-rate going forward, with pro-rata additions for new capex.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 phasing and utilisation for cables and conductors.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp will be gradual, with Q2 partly affected by rain and Q3–Q4 the strongest; utilisation is guided at ~40% for conductors and ~50–52% for cables in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin guidance and metal price sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 11–13% EBITDA margin, depending on metal prices; management cited aluminium moving from about $3,800 in May to about $3,000 by end-June. Mix is expected to improve as MV and EHV volumes rise in Q2–Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term debt and peak debt outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no substantial debt, the INR400 crore promoter unsecured loan has been repaid post-QIP and the INR1,900 crore promoter-held bonds are 0.01% payable after 30 years, with a net present value of INR47 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peer comparison given the flat Q-o-Q revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 softness to MV/EHV being laid at project sites that cannot be laid in rain, and said the peers' business is largely LV, so the cycle hits Diamond more.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration, including Adani.
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is about 40%+ of the order book, with a Board mandate to cut it to about 20% by year-end; the company is engaging about 670 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix at the INR14,000 crore peak and what could go wrong.
qa_highlights.answer: Conductors 30–35%, LV 10–15%, MV/EHV the remainder; data center target 20%, exports not yet sized beyond INR500 crore order target. Key risks are metal and polymer price moves requiring 20–30% more working capital, and execution capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crore, with management saying it is firmly on track and intends to hold the Q1 margin profile while delivering it.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11–13%, dependent on metal prices; management said the absolute contribution stays steady under price-escalation contracts.
Q1 seasonality: management said an on-time monsoon would have added INR70–80 crore of top line and corresponding EBITDA in Q1.
FY28 revenue target of INR7,500 crore; management said the full-utilisation potential of INR14,000 crore is not expected in FY29.
Data center sales targeted at about INR750 crore in FY27 and INR1,500 crore in FY28 (about 20% of revenue); internal target of INR1,000 crore data center orders before 31 Mar 2027.
Export order book target of at least INR500 crore by year-end FY27; management said export guidance beyond this will be given after year-end.
Management said it expects around INR300 crore of legacy NCLT receivables (out of INR957 crore) to be recovered over 12–18 months.
capex_capacity: Two aluminium corrugation lines approved by the board for 66 kV and 132 kV cable capacity; capex about INR17 crore, achieved by converting one 33 kV line.

Sixth CCV line being ordered this month at an agreed price; delivery assurance for August 2027, commissioning expected by December 2027 with no additional civil or utility capex. Management said it triples capability in the target segment.

Two additional medium voltage cable lines under installation, said to be on schedule; one silane line expected by 15 Sep 2026, fourth rod mill by 15 Oct 2026, and one CCV line in March 2027 (per Q&A).

Copper LV and control cable facility converting old rod mill and legacy conductor plant (brownfield, no civil cost), about 42,000 km capacity and revenue potential about INR1,880 crore at full utilisation; commercial production FY28, commissioning before March 2027.

Capex per line per Q&A: silane line INR15–20 crore; CCV line about INR50 crore for the line plus about INR50 crore utilities and civil (about INR100 crore total), with revenue of about INR45–50 crore per line. Utilisation guided at conductors ~40% and cables ~50–52% in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 across 12 product lines, about 2x last year's revenue; over INR1,000 crore of fresh wins since April and about INR400 crore of orders in the last 6–7 days.

Gujarat disaster-management programme (Robust) estimated at INR22,000 crore over three years, of which INR16,000 crore is 11 kV and 33 kV MV cable; Rajesh Power 1,370 km order from Paschim Gujarat; management expects INR4,000–5,000 crore of Gujarat orders to be finalised by year-end.

Working capital needs rising with metal and polymer costs and the need for vendor and dealer financing.
Customer concentration: Adani at 40%+ of the order book against the 20% target.
Monsoon and project-site disruption affecting MV/EHV laying in Q2 (described as partially affected).
key_quotes: We are completely back-to-back on passing the increases in metal and polymers to all our customers.

522163|2026-09.headline: Diamond Power Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,032 crore (up 135% YoY), with PAT of INR108 crore and net worth turned positive.
522163|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,032 crore, up 135% YoY and 50% QoQ, with EBITDA (incl. other income) of INR133 crore at a 12.9% margin and PAT of INR108 crore versus INR28 crore a year ago. Management attributed part of the growth to aluminium and copper price pass-through, estimating about one-third of revenue growth is metal and price variation, and pointed to a new data centre copper cable line contributing INR242 crore (23% of revenue). The balance sheet swung to positive net worth of INR764 crore and net cash of INR572 crore after the INR1,614 crore QIP and full repayment of promoter loans. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300-4,500 crore, implying INR2,580 crore in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is data centre cable revenue sustainable, and what is the margin difference versus conventional cables?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are price escalation based with a 30-day lag; falling metal prices lift percentage margin, and absolute contribution per unit is stable. No one-off costs were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margin expectations and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% EBITDA margin until polymer is on stream, then 14-16% from next year; capacity utilisation is about 45% of the level expected after full balancing equipment is operational.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy receivables are INR957 crore; it targets recovering INR300 crore within 24 months, of which INR116 crore is confirmed by customers so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax shield timeline?

risks_watch: H2 revenue of about INR2,580 crore must be delivered to meet guidance; execution depends on Q3-Q4 order inflows and the seasonal tender cycle.
About 43% of the order book is Adani Group; concentration risk and the stated 20% cap timeline are not defined.
Metal price swings (aluminium, copper) affect percentage margins; a 30-day pass-through lag creates about 1% EBITDA variance per management.
Polymer Phase 1 commissioning in June-December 2027 and Phase 2 in early 2028 are key to the 14-16% margin target; delays would defer it.
Legacy receivables of INR957 crore with INR300 crore targeted for recovery over 24 months; only INR116 crore confirmed so far.
Management commentary on competition intensity, quality undercutting in the market, and the 2028-2032 capacity plan (to be detailed at Q4 FY27) remain open.
522163|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, data centre demand and polymer integration, with specific numeric targets. Less precise on FY28 capacity additions, the industry growth rate and the 2028-2032 roadmap, which were deferred to Q4.
key_quotes: Our revenue grew by 135%. Metal and price variation pass-through account for perhaps a third of that. The rest is real.
For us, quality is our brand, and that is why our employee and other expenses are 5.7% of revenue, and that is why our savings goes completely to the bottom line.
I can only tell you that the margin which we are having presently is the most reasonable margin which you should expect from us.
So EBITDA margins will always remain between 11% to 13%. Once our polymer gets on stream by December 2027, in the next year we will like to give you a band of 14% to 16%.

522195|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 39.22% to ₹322.06 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.80%, with management guiding ~30% growth to ₹500 crore gross revenue in FY27.
522195|2026-03.overview: Frontier Springs delivered FY26 revenue from operations of ₹322.06 crore (up 39.22%), EBITDA of ₹86.31 crore (up 73.80%) and PAT of ₹61.31 crore (up 76.88%). Q4 revenue was ₹82.54 crore (up 17.7% YoY, marginally above Q3) with EBITDA margin of 28.51%. Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore on an order book it put at ₹300-370 crore, and says it expects to hold margins at 23-24% or higher, while acknowledging steel-cost pressure could trim 1-2 points. Q&A centred on margin guidance, the FIBA product launch, air spring capacity and wagon tenders.

financial_highlights.change: up 17.7% YoY; marginally ahead of Q3 FY26
margin up 362 bps QoQ-stated as YoY in call and 462 bps YoY in call; call states both 362 bps and 462 bps

segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited by management as approximately ₹175 crore plus (analyst's recollection, confirmed as approximate gross figure). Management expects reasonable growth in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross revenue target above ₹500 crore, described as around 30% growth, backed by an order book of ₹300-370 crore disclosed on the call.
Margin target of 23-24% for the year, with management saying 26-28% is possible; management conceded 1-2 points could be lost on existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Medium-term growth of 25% per year beyond FY27 was stated; management also said 20-25% average growth is achievable across the three product lines.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore across all three divisions, after about ₹20 crore in FY26; no term loans taken in several years.

Q4 FY27 is expected to be the strongest quarter, with the 6-ton hammer contributing from the third quarter onward; management expects the first-half revenue run-rate to break out of the ₹80-83 crore band.
capex_capacity: Air spring capacity 300 coach sets per month, utilisation 180-200 per month (about 60-67%); final testing is the bottleneck, and two more testing machines are planned.

A 6-ton forging hammer was installed in FY26, joining 1-ton and 3-ton hammers; utilisation is one 8-hour shift out of 16 hours available.
FY27 capex of ₹20-25 crore across coil, air and forging divisions, focused on capacity and less manpower-intensive automation.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is ₹300-370 crore, mostly Railways. Orders come in daily, mainly small, and are not individually disclosed; the company agreed to post larger orders on the exchanges.

Railways' production plan for FY27 is about 6,000 passenger coaches and 1,200-1,400 locomotives, flat YoY; a large wagon tender is expected, with forging and springs supply.
Competition: no new spring or forging players, though more steel suppliers have been added by Railways, improving sourcing terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between pass-through of commodity costs and the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing tenders at fixed prices may be lower; if the year completes, margin could fall by 1-2 points, but management aims to hold current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility for FY28-29 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific figure yet; management sees no order scarcity for 5-10 years and said growth of 25% is expected beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 revenue by division and air spring capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate gross figures: coil springs ₹175 crore plus, forging ₹60 crore plus, air springs ₹150 crore; air spring output 180-190 coach sets per month against 300 capacity.

qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks include delayed inspections by Railways inspectors and occasional raw material delays; management expects to break out in Q1 FY27.

Air spring testing bottleneck and whether two more testing machines are commissioned in time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: The Gulf war raised raw material costs and shipping costs (about 4x). The company had requested price increases from export OEM customers but put them on hold when prices fell, and has not taken an increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US OEM growth outlook and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects US business to grow substantially over three years, through wallet share gains with Ford and Chrysler and new Europe RFQs. It declined to give an order book figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company should look at annual margin, which can move 1-2% either way quarter to quarter; it aims to maintain the margin level guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is 65-66% on a 48 million meter total capacity basis (PVC 3.5-3.7 million meters per month); the new line lifts capacity to about 4-4.2 million meters per month and gives 25-30% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the PU plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The PU plant is underutilised with no change in three months. Sampling with top brands has been done but no business is confirmed, and management cannot make a strong recommendation this financial year.

risks_watch: Freight and raw material costs: shipping cost reportedly up about 4x and raw material prices volatile since March 2026; company has not taken a price increase on export OEM business, so the margin recovery depends on timing of price hikes and freight easing.
US export pricing: a price increase was requested from US customers but not pushed hard; outcome depends on market moves over the next two to three weeks, per management.
Capex and overseas plant: FY27 capex about INR50 crore; a further roughly INR250 crore over two years depends on an overseas plant location not yet finalised (Mexico, US or other NAFTA).
Volume growth: total volume only about 2.77%, domestic about 1%; footwear de-grew on sole price increases; growth guidance of 10-15% is leaning on exports.
PU plant: underutilised with no change for three months, no confirmed business from top brands, and no firm recommendation for this financial year.

key_quotes: So, we have not taken a price increase in the export market but you also have to look at one more thing in this 10% more or less natural hedge has happened.
So, we have a headroom to expand to 25%, 30% more capacity.
So anywhere between 10% to 15% growth, we are not looking very strong growth in the domestic market. But yes, we are looking at a very strong growth in the export market.
But this present quarter's margin will be sustainable and expected to continue.

522249|2026-09.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% to INR282.95 crore and PAT 42% to INR57.99 crore, helped by warehouse stock clearance in the US.
522249|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR282.95 crore (up 18% YoY), with PBT of INR79.31 crore (up 43%) and PAT of INR57.99 crore (up 42%). Standalone revenue was INR252.99 crore (up 6%), with PBT of INR70.46 crore (up 9%) and PAT of INR51.27 crore (up 7%). Management attributed the consolidated outperformance to lower dispatches from India and higher sales from the US warehouse, which cleared its own stock. Export OEM volumes were weak YoY because US auto demand softened, though management said orders are in hand and the trend is improving. Management declined to give formal guidance for the second half or FY28, and the Executive Director was absent from the call due to a family bereavement.

financial_highlights.value: INR90.46 crore (General INR33 crore; OEM INR57.46 crore)
OEM INR62.80 crore; Replacement INR45.02 crore; Footwear INR45.34 crore; Furnishing INR7.19 crore; Others INR2.18 crore; Domestic total INR162.53 crore

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ due to Q1 labour-code provision reversal in Q2

segments.name: Export OEM (standalone)
segments.commentary: INR57.46 crore in Q2, below the INR75-80 crore run-rate cited by an analyst; management said it is improving. Volumes were up 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ, though the export volume YoY was negative per management.

segments.name: Export General
segments.commentary: INR33 crore in Q2. Management expects double-digit improvement, supported by a newly started retail arm in Europe.

segments.name: Domestic auto replacement
segments.commentary: INR45.02 crore in Q2. Volume grew about 11% QoQ and about 5% YoY.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR45.34 crore in Q2. Management said volume and value both rose, and guided to 5-10% annual volume growth. Focus is on selected, higher-margin customers.

segments.name: Furnishing
segments.commentary: INR7.19 crore in Q2. Retail is facing price competition; about 750-800 sub-dealers and 8-10 distributors were appointed.

segments.name: PU (polyurethane)
segments.commentary: Revenue booked INR6.28 crore in Q2. Management said the segment is not profitable and operates at about 25% utilisation versus about 40% needed for breakeven.

guidance_outlook: Export OEM expected at INR250-300 crore in FY27 (consolidated basis), versus about INR260-280 crore in FY26 after a confused exchange on the figure.
Export OEM expected to return to INR75-80 crore per quarter from the current level, with improvement described as gradual rather than dated.
Gross margin sustainable at about 55-56%, with variation tied to raw material and crude prices.
No guidance given for H2 FY27 or FY28 top-line or bottom-line; management said the current margin should hold and top-line growth around 20% should continue.
Export OEM expected to grow 10-15% in the following two years, per management.
capex_capacity: New machinery for an additional line: equipment expected in late November to December 2026, installation to begin in the March 2027 quarter, with operations starting in Q1 FY28.
A new plant in India is under consideration, especially in the South region; a Mexico plant is in the pipeline but not concluded.
Capacity utilisation is unchanged QoQ; PU business is at about 25% utilisation against about 40% needed for breakeven.
Bhadla mini-grid solar investment: management cited a payback period of at most 2 years.
demand_pricing: US auto demand weak for two quarters; OEMs revised projections and Q2 US dispatches were deliberately reduced, with warehouse stock cleared instead.
US OEM orders expanded to 5 models from 2 for Ford and Chrysler; BMW and Mercedes-Benz (export OEM) are taking material close to full projections.
Freight and PVC costs spiked from the West Asia conflict and are now easing; management will not pass costs to export customers until increases look stable and permanent.
Footwear and furnishing domestic markets face high price competition; management is deprioritising footwear in favour of higher-margin auto exports.
Pipeline includes VW, plus leather accessories talks in the Kolkata and Kanpur belt; management said new OEM wins take 2-3 years to convert.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of export and domestic auto OEM volume growth, and reasons for weak export volumes.
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic replacement volume grew about 11% QoQ and 5% YoY; OEM volume grew 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ. Export volume was negative YoY because US customers delayed new car purchases; the warehouse cleared its own stock.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other income fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had an extra provision for labour-code changes that was reversed in Q2, so underlying employee cost is about INR12.5 crore per quarter. Other income fell QoQ due to fair-value losses on treasury investments; YoY it rose.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability given volatility (Q1 about 52%, Q2 about 57%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 55-56% as sustainable, with variation driven by raw material and crude prices.

qa_highlights.question: Transfer pricing between India and the US warehouse subsidiary.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiary keeps the margin needed to cover its local costs and the rest is billed to the subsidiary. Example given: a 10% margin split 8% India and 2% US subsidiary. When consolidated revenue exceeds standalone, the consolidated margin is higher.

qa_highlights.question: Export OEM size and FY26 base: analyst cited INR285-290 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said about INR200 crore for FY26, then about INR260 crore, then confirmed about INR280 crore on a consolidated basis, with FY27 expected at INR250-300 crore. The numbers were inconsistent on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning after the AGM resolution was not passed.
qa_highlights.answer: The board discussed it; the resolution will be re-proposed with a revised structure after the remuneration and perquisite terms were objected to. A third generation joined about 6 months ago, but Manav Poddar is not directly running the business at present.

risks_watch: Export OEM recovery depends on US OEM schedules; the Q2 export volume decline YoY was attributed to customers delaying new car purchases.
Consolidated growth was flattered by warehouse stock clearance; watch whether standalone growth catches up in Q3 and Q4.
PU segment remains loss-making at about 25% utilisation, with breakeven at about 40%; tax benefits are masking the loss.
Inconsistent export OEM figures given on the call (INR200 crore, INR260 crore, INR280 crore) need reconciliation in the next disclosure.
Governance: AGM resolution not passed and must be re-tabled; Executive Director absent from call; succession still open.
Gross margin is volatile, tied to crude and raw material prices; freight and PVC costs may rebound.
522249|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins and the US/South Africa OEM pipeline, but evasive on forward numbers: no guidance for H2 FY27 or FY28, and several figures (export OEM base, transfer pricing) were corrected or left unclear during Q&A.
key_quotes: Basically, market is not responding well in U.S. for last 2 quarters.
So the sale, which increased is because of clearance of the stock from warehouse and in comparison to dispatch from India.
PU, it's not, in fact, generating profit just -- but we are managing because of some tax benefits and all.

522275|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
522275|2026-03.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.
522275|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, backlog and margins, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance on HVDC phasing, pipeline timing and export mix, and said quarterly order intake can be lumpy.
key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

522275|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
522275|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

financial_highlights.change: -2.5% QoQ from INR214.6 billion at March 2026
vs 48.4% a year ago and 47% in Q4 FY26; FY26 full year 45.3%

financial_highlights.metric: Total available cash incl. cash pool lending

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export orders about INR5.2 billion of the INR11.4 billion Q1 intake; management says 80-90% of export orders come from GE Vernova group entities. Exports are 10-15% of backlog.

segments.name: Domestic TBCB and grid
segments.commentary: Third-party orders about INR6.5 billion in Q1, per management. Private customers are 77% of backlog, central utilities and PSUs 21%, state utilities 2%.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: Backlog is back-ended; meaningful growth expected from FY29 onward. Developers' first-phase bids for the next HVDC projects are expected to be decided in August or September 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at mid-20s.
Management stated it remains confident of the INR7,000-8,000 crore annual base order flow guidance, although Q1 base orders were about INR1,100 crore.
Domestic TBCB market expected flat or up 6-7% in FY27; double-digit growth not expected.
Backlog about 3.5x FY26 revenue; growth to be non-linear, with healthy growth in FY27 and FY28 and a step-up from FY29 on HVDC.
INR10 billion capacity expansion already announced; INR2.5 billion dividend planned in Q2 subject to shareholder approval; about INR16 billion of surplus cash with no firm allocation.
Chinese GIS suppliers recently approved for Indian market; impact on pricing and orders unclear until private TBCB negotiations start.
capex_capacity: INR10 billion capacity expansion programme announced in FY26, mostly inside existing plants on land already owned.
Vallam project (INR55 crore): part of capacity expected in Q1 CY27, balance by end-2027 (management said 'Q1 of 27' and 'end of 27'), against an earlier December 2026 target.
Capex on existing plants said to be tracking on schedule; management says it will not affect capacity utilisation.
Utilisation: some factories heavily loaded, others have room to grow.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake down 30% YoY on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026; management says June-July TBCB pipeline is better, but the timing of conversion into orders is uncertain.

INR3,000 crore RPT order (a transformer project in the US per the call, though Q&A is unclear on the location) is on hold at the customer; approval lapses at the September AGM and would need re-validation. Management said it is not lost.
INR1,300 crore US data-centre RPT order not booked; expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after location and state change.
Data-centre orders are not significant in the current book; larger high-voltage data-centre projects are under discussion.

Commodity pass-through: transformers and HVDC carry IEEMA-linked escalation formulas; other turnkey work (CRGO and similar) is priced on forecast commodity costs with an 18-24 month order-to-execution lag.
Competition: Chinese GIS players approved; Tier-2 competition is limited in GIS and circuit breakers but present in other products.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore RPT orders being booked, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: None of the INR1,300 crore order is booked; it is expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27. The INR3,000 crore project is on hold at the customer over budget issues and would need fresh shareholder approval after the September AGM. Management said both are not lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in export orders, and what is the RPT pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline improved on US utility demand for instrument transformers and 400 kV GIS opportunities. Management declined to comment on the new RPT pipeline beyond saying it will go to shareholders when projects become live.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin bridge from 45.3% FY26 gross margin to 41.3% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2-2.5 points from ramp-up of lower-margin HV business (offset at EBITDA level); 1-1.5 points from lower export share and a high-margin export order in FY26; and the rest from lower execution savings due to elevated commodity prices. EBITDA was 25.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the mid-20s EBITDA guidance intact, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-20s EBITDA guidance for FY27 is maintained. Transformers have formula-based escalation; other turnkey work relies on forecast costs, so cost pressure shows up in execution 1-2 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power Grid TBCB timeline stretching to 24-30 months a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not affect capacity utilisation; ordering cycles may lengthen by about 3-4 months for longer tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What will the company do with surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are under evaluation and nothing is firm; announced uses are INR10 billion capex and INR2.5 billion dividend, leaving about INR16 billion unallocated.

risks_watch: Order intake: Q1 down 30% YoY; FY27 base order flow target of INR7,000-8,000 crore needs a sharp pick-up from Q1 run-rate of about INR1,100 crore.
Gross margin: 41.3% in Q1 vs 45.3% FY26; commodity cost pressure lags into execution over 18-24 months.
RPT timing: INR3,000 crore project on hold and needs re-approval after the September AGM; INR1,300 crore US data-centre order not yet booked.
HVDC pipeline slippage (South Kalamb and others) and back-ended execution until FY29.
Chinese GIS suppliers entering the Indian market may pressure pricing and share, especially in private TBCB.
Surplus cash of about INR16 billion is unallocated; capital allocation decision still pending.

522275|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR20.3 billion and EBITDA margin hit 27.1%, the top of the mid-20s guidance band, with net zero debt.
522275|2026-09.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR20.3 billion, up 32% YoY, with H1 revenue of INR38.6 billion, up 35%. Q2 order intake was INR24.4 billion, up 52% YoY, taking H1 intake to about INR35.8 billion (up 11%), and order backlog ended at INR214.4 billion. EBITDA was INR5.5 billion (27.1% of revenue) and PAT was INR4.3 billion (21.3%), with cash and equivalents of about INR32.5 billion. Management reiterated mid-20s EBITDA guidance for the full year and said HVDC execution will mostly start from FY28, while two related-party export orders are on hold or pending.

segments.name: Transmission equipment (single segment)
segments.commentary: Company reports one segment (high-voltage transmission products), so no split for software and services; management said that share may have dropped as equipment orders grew faster.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share was 21% of Q2 orders and 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 export share was 29% of orders and 31% of revenue. Management says export orders carry higher margin than domestic, by about 500 bps as previously indicated.

guidance_outlook: Mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance maintained for FY27; H1 EBITDA was about 26.2%.
No significant HVDC execution revenue expected in FY27 or the next financial year; significant HVDC contribution expected from FY28.
Management does not give gross margin guidance and does not share long-range guidance; FY27 base order expectation of INR70-80 billion was kept unchanged.
Expects revenue growth of more than 30% a year over the next three years, supported by backlog plus HVDC L1 position, with about INR10 billion capacity expansion.
Expects at least 2-3 HVDC projects to come in the next year; a sizable STATCOM order is expected in Q4.
Expects data-center traction to strengthen from Q4 or next year; India data-center share of backlog is less than 2%.
risks_watch: Two related-party export orders (about INR31 billion lapsed; US $151 million approval valid to 15 May 2027) depend on customer timing and are not in backlog.
Supply-chain risk: management called it the top operational risk; 765 kV bushings are mostly imported with lead times above 15-18 months.
Revenue mix shifting toward equipment and away from services; no segment disclosure for software and services.
Pricing pressure on regular high-voltage transformers, while copper prices have risen sharply.
Timing of HVDC execution (mostly FY28 onward) and its margin profile, which management has not guided.
522275|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order flow, margins and execution, but guarded on forward specifics: management declined gross margin and long-range guidance, and gave vague timing on the held related-party orders, Trench synergies and competition.
key_quotes: We are confident of converting our INR214 billion backlog profitably over the coming years.
So, for the entire year, Aditya, we will maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA margin.
