qa_highlights.question: Will the parent's Trench acquisition and planned Trench manufacturing in India be part of GE Vernova T&D India, and what is the services and software revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on Trench as the deal closes later in FY27. It does not disclose services and software revenue because it reports one segment; the share may have dropped as equipment orders grew faster.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 2 related-party export orders on hold likely to clear in 6-12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: The customer put the hold on due to bigger project size and it is unclear whether it lifts in 6, 8 or 12 months, so too early to speculate. The US related-party order is in discussion, with a hope to conclude in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin be sustained at the high level for the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company will maintain mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance for the full year. Management declined to guide on gross margin, which it said varies quarter to quarter by mix, and H1 EBITDA was about 26.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Barmer HVDC order hurt EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution is expected over the next 2-4 financial years, with no significant HVDC execution revenue in FY27 and no significant contribution next year; significant HVDC revenue starts from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is any part of the backlog cancelled due to data-centre issues, and what is the sensed market risk?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said there is no sense of any cancellation and that he was not aware of such queries. India data-centre share of backlog is less than 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook once HVDC execution starts, given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO clarified gross margin is around 45% in Q2, not 55%-57%. He declined to give gross margin guidance, citing operating leverage and mix, and said long-range guidance will be communicated later.

capex_capacity: Capacity expansion programme of about INR10 billion (also referred to as INR1,100 crore capex); roughly 20% already incurred as of the call.
Management says more than 90% of the investment is in existing plants where land is already held, giving integrated expansion with lower capex need than peers for similar volume.
Utilisation at most factories described as pretty high; asked whether above 75%, CEO answered yes.
Localisation: HVDC transformers, thyristor valves and controls now manufactured in India; sub-vendor components such as CRGO and oil still imported; localisation to be taken component by component.
765 kV bushings mostly imported; domestic capacity limited but expansion under way; 765 kV bushing lead times more than 15-18 months, transformer build 3-4 months.
Asia has two transformer factories per management: Indonesia (up to 245 kV) and Vadodara (higher ratings).

Commissioned in Q2: 400 kV substation for NEA Nepal, 400 kV GIS at Babarzar (GETCO), 765 kV reactors for PGCIL at Bidar and Resonia at Beawar, 765 kV generator transformer for NUPPL at Ghatampur, GIS at Narela Delhi, export jobs in Spain and Senegal.
demand_pricing: Q2 order intake INR24.4 billion (+52% YoY vs INR16.1 billion); H1 order intake about INR35.8 billion (+11%); backlog INR214.4 billion at Sept 2026 vs INR214.6 billion at March 2026, said to be more than 3 years of revenue.

Key Q2 wins: 400 kV generator transformer and 420 kV GIS for a 1,500 MW pumped storage project in Maharashtra; 800 kV and 420 kV GIS for Andhra Pradesh transmission; 400 kV reactors and 420/220 kV GIS for a TBCB project in Himachal Pradesh; 765 kV shunt reactor for a TBCB project in Andhra Pradesh.
Export share: 21% of Q2 orders and 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 29% of orders and 31% of revenue. H1 export orders INR10.4 billion, largely related-party, vs INR11.8 billion in full FY26.

Two related-party export approvals: about INR31 billion for HV switchgear components to Middle East and France customers lapsed at 2026 AGM (customer hold); US entity approval for about $151 million valid to 15 May 2027, order in discussion, hoped to conclude in H2 FY27. Neither is in backlog.
Domestic pipeline: lowest bidder for Power Grid Barmer HVDC (awarded to Power Grid); strong TBCB pipeline over last 3-4 months; management expects strong pipeline for next 4-5 months.

Pricing: slight pressure on regular high-voltage transformer prices, described as very little; no HVDC tender since Barmer, so no competitive-intensity read on HVDC. Management did not see the copper-driven pricing uplift that an analyst expected.
Export orders carry higher margin than domestic, about 500 bps, trend unchanged per management.
Data centres: India data-centre installed base about 1.5 GW, expected 8-10 GW by 2030; India data-centre share of backlog less than 2%; stronger traction expected from Q4 or next year.
Trench acquisition by parent (announced about two days before the call) expected to close in later part of FY27; management said too early to comment on India integration.

522295|2026-03.headline: Control Print FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose to INR482 crores from INR425 crores; CP Italy (V-Shapes) packaging losses remain the key concern.
522295|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR484 crores (vs INR431 crores) and standalone Q4 total revenue of about INR138 crores (vs INR114 crores). Standalone coding and marking drove growth, with management attributing most of the increase to volume and a small part to price, and a surcharge introduced to offset input cost pressure. The call was dominated by questions on losses at the Italian subsidiary V-Shapes (CP Italy), which management attributed almost entirely to the packaging business, and on the rationale for new IP and track-and-trace investments. Management said V-Shapes losses should fall in FY27 and could approach breakeven, though no firm timeline was given.

segments.name: Coding and marking (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management calls it the main profit centre; Q4 revenue mix was printers 12%, consumables 62%, spares 9%, services 16%. FY26 mix was printers 14%, consumables 61%, spares 9%, services 15%. Management expects a reasonably good year in FY27.

segments.name: Track and Trace
segments.commentary: Management says the conventional business is at breakeven or slightly profitable; no figures disclosed. Two pilots with top 5-10 Indian pharma companies are nearing completion, with a possible scale-up if results succeed.

segments.name: Packaging (India and overseas)
segments.commentary: Management cited good traction in core packing, with a pipeline for laminates, food packing and new machines. A new UNNATI packaging-material plant is planned at Guwahati to lower material costs.

segments.name: CP Italy / V-Shapes (packaging machines)
segments.commentary: Management says the subsidiary accounts for almost all consolidated overseas losses. Loss for FY26 was guided at about EUR1.5 million, down from EUR2-2.5 million in FY25. Machine quality issues and the inability to ship machines to Gulf customers have delayed revenue.

segments.name: CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT
segments.commentary: Management says these are at breakeven or better, with 15-20% growth expected for each; CODEOLOGY is being restructured to a smaller core business, and MARKPRINT has contracts in hand. No subsidiary-level sales or profit figures were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: V-Shapes losses expected to reduce in FY26/FY27, with breakeven possible this year per management; no firm commitment.

Management said no further major equity infusion into V-Shapes is needed after the current IP and inventory conversion, though a planned EUR-denominated IP and equity infusion of about INR32 crores into the Italian subsidiary was raised by an analyst.
CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT expected to grow about 15-20% a year.
Surcharge to customers to continue until the end of the calendar year to offset cost increases.

Guwahati UNNATI plant to cut packaging material costs by about 40% (from about INR2-2.5 per pack to about INR1.5 or lower) and is supported by incentives including INR7.5 crores capital subsidy, 5% interest subvention for six years and GST refund over 10 years.
capex_capacity: Guwahati UNNATI packaging-material plant planned in the Northeast, for which management cited incentives: a capital subsidy of INR7.5 crores on a INR15 crore plant and machinery investment (capped), 5% interest subvention for six years, and a GST refund over 10 years equal to plant and machinery investment.
CP Italy batch of 10 machines being finalized; first two machines had quality and specification issues, and the company is supplying stock machines from India to customers in the interim.
Management says V-Shapes is sourcing parts from local Italian suppliers at higher cost and plans to move sourcing to India to reduce costs in batches.
Print-and-apply and thermal transfer print engine being developed under CODEOLOGY; first sales expected in FY27.
Management said Guwahati expansion uses existing plot and is a minor expansion in an existing plant with spare capacity.
demand_pricing: Management said price hikes were implemented and a customer surcharge was introduced to recover input costs; the price hike size was not quantified.
Management attributed the Q4 standalone growth mainly to volume, with some cost-driven price increases.

Management said the Indian coding and marking market is about INR2,000-2,200 crores, growing about 10% a year, and that packaging-sector (pharma, F&B, FMCG) demand is stable while industrial demand fluctuates more.
Gulf and Middle East customers of V-Shapes stopped buying as shipments to the Strait of Hormuz area were blocked.

Management said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores, and that pharma serialization (top 300 drugs, possibly extended to 946) is a driver, though there is no notification yet on the extension.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Garg: Are the international acquisition losses a repeat of past vanity acquisitions, and what are the cumulative loss and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiva Kabra said the losses are almost entirely in the overseas packaging business (CP Italy) and that the programme has milestones; the investment cycle is longer than expected because the machines needed more stabilisation. He said the IP is now held by Control Print rather than CP Italy and could be licensed. No cumulative loss or investment figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Madhur Rathi: What drove the rise in standalone employee benefit expense from about INR21 crores to INR27-28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Barve said the new wage code (effective November 2025) required a recast of leave-encashment and gratuity liabilities, about INR3.5 crores in impact. Provisions were also made for sales incentives and key management loyalty bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Thakur: When will V-Shapes break even, and will losses stop after FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said V-Shapes losses were about EUR2-2.5 million in FY25 and were guided to about EUR1.5 million this year; breakeven could come this year. He said little further funding is needed after current inventory ships, though some loans to V-Shapes will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the nature of the losses and the course correction for V-Shapes?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said about half of V-Shapes costs are R&D, and the rest is contract packaging plus manufacturing and sales. Fixed operating costs were estimated at about USD2-2.5 million per year, with total costs of about EUR2-3 million. Three to four non-productive staff have been let go; investment is going into sales.

qa_highlights.question: Saloni Arya: When do losses subside, what is the Track and Trace market size and margin, and what is the V-Shapes investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores; pilots are with two large pharma companies. He said margins are at least similar to the coding and marking gross margin, with no numerical margin disclosed. No cumulative V-Shapes investment was given.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Singh: Where are the quality issues at CP Italy, and what is the total cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the first machines needed multiple engineering visits and the second was swapped for stock, so the company is aiming for 10 identical machines. Jaideep Barve said the CP Italy total cost is about EUR750,000 a year in direct wages, and Kabra said total fixed operating cost is about USD2-2.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Nikunj Bhanushali: What were the FY26 sales and P&L of CODEOLOGY, MARKPRINT and CP Italy, and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose subsidiary sales or profit figures; said the entire consolidated overseas loss is CP Italy. Kabra guided CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT to 15-20% growth and said CODEOLOGY will be scaled down for margin. FY26 printer sales were about 3,064.

522295|2026-06.headline: Control Print standalone operating revenue rose about 5% to ₹105 crore in Q1 FY27, with V-Shapes packaging still loss-making and breakeven pushed to H1 FY28.
522295|2026-06.overview: Standalone total revenue was about ₹107 crore and operating revenue about ₹105 crore versus ₹100 crore a year earlier, with Coding & Marking about 95% of operating revenue. Management attributed the slow quarter to extrusion and pipes demand softness, polymer price volatility linked to the Iran conflict, and a slower consumables pull-through. Consolidated operating revenue was about ₹115 crore against ₹111 crore, with COGS at about 43% versus 42%. The packaging subsidiary (V-Shapes/CP Italy) remains a drag: management now expects the Packaging business to break even only in H1 FY28, and disclosed no new subsidiary cash infusion beyond a planned IP transfer purchase.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the actual tax outgo is already reflected, and the higher deferred tax is a timing difference from capex-driven tax vs accounting depreciation. It said the annual tax rate is in line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a domestic/export revenue split annually?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider providing the split, possibly offline, but did not commit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pickup in recyclable film demand, and how is Creative progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic recyclable film demand is weak until the government mandates recyclable packaging. Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management aims for cash and net profit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and is there a plan to expand into new sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, and calibrated given uncertainty. Management said it adds one or two customers almost every month across sectors and is not sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 margins be higher with Chennai and cylinder ramp-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty. It said margins should improve with better utilisation if conditions are better.

qa_highlights.question: Is paper cost still rising, and what is the impact of the minimum import price on board?
qa_highlights.answer: Paper cost pressure continues, with virgin board up sharply and recycled board rising steadily. The MIP on board imports gives domestic mills some room, and management expects some price increase is inevitable.

ECB mark-to-market exposure to euro movements could keep adding to finance cost.

Monitor utilisation at Chennai, the cylinder facility and the fourth flexible line, plus the Creative break-even trajectory.
Fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit domestic consumer demand in coming quarters.

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.
523301|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 18%. Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

domestic growth at good double-digit clip

qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise by ~30% at an investment of INR 50-60 crore; existing capacity is almost fully utilised.

qa_highlights.answer: No. The prior-year quarter included a one-time forex/mark-to-market loss; this quarter is a normalised comparison. Debt figure not given.

523329|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings rose 120% to INR 744 crores on Solano Gardens launch, while Q4 margins were hit by about INR 14 crores of one-off expenses.
523329|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 bookings of INR 744 crores (up 120% YoY) and collections of INR 352.1 crores (up ~39%), driven by the Solano Gardens launch where 343 of 433 units sold for over INR 384 crores. Q4 FY26 booking value was INR 382.7 crores and collections INR 96.5 crores. Q4 profitability was dented by about INR 14 crores of one-time items (GST input write-off of ~INR 11 crores plus earlier-project costs). The company added ~INR 2,000 crores GDV through three Lucknow land parcels, two via LDA auctions, and guided to ~INR 4,000 crores total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects over 5 to 7 years.

Vinyl PBDIT rose sharply to Rs 51 crore from Rs 12 crore, while Bioseed posted a Rs 41 crore loss. Management declared a 200% interim dividend (Rs 62.38 crore) and flagged a demerger targeted for Q1 FY28 board consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth profitability drop sharply, and will employee costs as a share of revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower transactional revenue and gestation of 100+ RMs hired in 18 months, who take 2.5-3 years to turn profitable. Management said headcount has likely peaked, with hiring now selective.

qa_highlights.question: Asset management SIP book down about 30% and AUM flat; what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-liquid AUM rose 16% QoQ; decline was linked to small/mid-cap concentration. Management engaged more distributors and expects SIP and AUM to recover over the next couple of quarters. Quantitative targets to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROE is achievable excluding market peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ROE was about 11.5%, constrained by the 50% NBFC payout cap. Management expects a similar or better range this year, with stronger ROE from Wealth and AMC operating leverage in about 2 years; CACM is about 15% ROE in a weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Private Markets carries 60-65% of capital and drags ROE; will capital mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is at a low of 0.8x and will rise toward 2x in about 3 years as syndication grows, lifting ROE into the teens. Dividends constrained to 50% of NBFC profits.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 Private Markets revenue came from the single large ARC transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC income is lumpy and largely booked on resolution; the June quarter included a big resolution, while book value fell by about INR1,200 crores of recovery and about INR600 crores was redeployed.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for demerger or listing of wealth and asset management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth and AM are still small; it will evaluate a listing or demerger at scale, subject to no tax leakage. Affordable housing listing is planned in 2-3 years.

523694|2026-03.headline: Apcotex Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 42% YoY to INR 55 crore at a 13.76% margin, with PAT up 107% to INR 35 crore.
523694|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR 398 crore (+14% YoY) on 10% volume growth, with EBITDA margin of 13.76% and PAT margin of 8.73%. FY26 delivered record sales volumes (+14% YoY) and record exports, but revenue grew only 4% to INR 1,442 crore while EBITDA hit a record INR 177 crore. Q4 included about INR 14 crore of employee-benefit provisions, INR 4 crore turbine impairment and INR 2 crore extra depreciation, which management called largely one-off. Management said the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure created short-term margin gains in Nitrile latex and some export disruption, and it did not give quarterly guidance.

segments.commentary: Running at 100% utilisation for several quarters and expected to stay full for about four more quarters until new capacity arrives in Q1 of the following fiscal year (FY28). The expansion will almost double NBR capacity.

segments.name: ApcoBuild
segments.commentary: Management expects double-digit growth after a manpower issue early in FY26 was corrected and the distribution channel was reviewed; the division ended the year strong.

segments.name: Synthetic latex
segments.commentary: New capacity is being built and is expected to come on stream in FY28, with some headroom in the existing plants.

segments.name: Middle East exports
segments.commentary: About 12% of total revenue, covering UAE, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey. Management says the business is good but margins have been hit by freight and raw material cost increases.

segments.name: Europe and US
segments.commentary: About 2-4% of revenue combined.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average, though quarter-on-quarter progression is uncertain.
FY27 volume growth expected in low double digits for the full year, against capacity that is already running near full. Revenue growth depends on raw material prices and is not guided.
Nitrile latex: no capacity addition in FY27. Debottlenecking will add a little. Major capacity lands in Q1 FY28.

Raw material cover is in place through end-June 2026. The company is not taking a view on crude or petrochemical prices.
Management expects a 2026 new R&D centre spend of INR 20-25 crore; there is no stated timeline for ADD relief.
capex_capacity: NBR expansion will almost double NBR capacity, with new capacity due in Q1 of FY28.

Synthetic latex: new capacity being built, expected in FY28, with headroom in existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 13-14 crore employee benefit provision and why did depreciation change?
qa_highlights.answer: Three items: a new five-year long-term incentive plan (INR 2.7 crore for the year, now expensed quarterly), pending litigation provision on external legal advice, and a gratuity policy change tied to the new wage code. Depreciation on co-gen assets was cut from 40 to 15 years because the turbine is idle, and the Valia turbine was impaired by about INR 4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 EBITDA the new base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance is given. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than the FY26 average at higher utilisation, but quarterly progression is uncertain given the war and raw material volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is structural versus temporary?

qa_highlights.question: Net cash position and non-recurring items?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nitrile latex contribution to FY26 revenue and EBITDA?

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Low double-digit volume growth for the full year if demand holds and capacity allows. Revenue growth is not guided because pricing is unknown.

523694|2026-06.headline: Apcotex Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 526 crore (+40% YoY) and PAT rose 311% to Rs 79 crore, helped by price realisations and inventory gains.
523694|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of Rs 526 crore, up 40% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 117 crore (22.3% margin vs 10.3%) and PAT of Rs 79 crore (15.01% margin vs 5.11%). Volumes fell 10-12% because exports to the MENA region were hit by West Asia disruption, freight costs and logistics issues, while domestic volumes rose about 10%. Management said inventory gains added roughly 2% to EBITDA margin. Working capital rose on higher raw material prices, and net cash fell to about Rs 40 crore from about Rs 70 crore at March 2026 (Q&A noted a figure of about Rs 30 crore).

segments.name: Nitrile latex (NBR/XNBR)
segments.commentary: Margins improved in Q1 versus prior years; management said they were above 15% in Q1 but did not reach that level through FY25-26. NBR is capacity-constrained with ~30% Indian market share, the rest met by imports.

segments.name: Synthetic latex / other products
segments.commentary: Management said margins expanded across all segments in Q1, not just nitrile latex. Company cites about 25 new products added and eight end-industries served.

segments.name: Apco build (small segment)
segments.commentary: Described as growing but still a small part of the business; no numbers given.

guidance_outlook: Average EBITDA margin guidance remains 15-16%; management declined to call Q1 margins sustainable and said it expects some quarters lower and some higher.
NBR capacity expansion expected on stream by Q1 FY28 (possibly April 2028); SB latex and other synthetic latex capex about a couple of months later (around June 2028).

Combined capex of about Rs 220 crore (Rs 130-140 crore for NBR debottlenecking/expansion adding roughly 100% of NBR capacity, rest for synthetic latex). Management expects about Rs 600 crore additional top line, roughly 40% uplift from announced projects.
Decision on a third (stage two) nitrile latex expansion expected in 3-4 months, after watching margins and Asian/Malaysian capacity.
Management expects volumes to rebound quickly once the West Asia conflict eases; said volumes in MENA may not grow near term while oil prices stay high.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 220 crore is in progress; only 15-20% spent so far, mainly advances and civil work. Major equipment deliveries are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
NBR debottlenecking/expansion costs Rs 130-140 crore and adds nearly 100% of current NBR capacity; original estimate was Rs 200-250 crore.
Plants run on dual fuel (gas and coal), and each raw material has multiple sources.
Capex so far is self-funded; management expects to take debt in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell 10-12% YoY and QoQ, entirely due to exports; MENA customers were hit by Strait of Hormuz disruption. Domestic volumes rose about 10%.

Realisations were higher in Q1, but management said they started falling late in the quarter as oil and raw material prices eased. It expects another price rise in August-September if crude rises again.
Domestic demand described as strong across paper, construction, rubber goods and others. Ocean freight costs were absorbed by the company on exports.

Competition: no anti-dumping duty in India currently. Management said Europe and the US have no NBR expansion announced; some Asian expansions are coming but expected to be absorbed in three to five years.
Working capital rose because of higher raw material values. Inventory days were unchanged; the increase came from price, not quantity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin came from inventory gains, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains added about 2% to EBITDA margin. Management now talks about average margins of 15-16%, not a sustainable level, and said the next few quarters may be lower or higher.

qa_highlights.question: What made the business resilient this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited deliberate investments in dual fuel, multiple raw material sources, quick procurement and inventory planning. It said these had been built over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Can throughput double in five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Announced projects should add about Rs 600 crore to top line, roughly 40%. Further doubling depends on market support, and management sees no reason it cannot happen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the NBR expansion approved now?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex fell to Rs 130-140 crore for almost 100% NBR capacity via debottlenecking, from Rs 200-250 crore earlier. Margins had improved and there is no major NBR expansion globally, so returns were justified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and capex spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash of about Rs 40 crore, down from about Rs 70 crore at March, partly due to higher working capital. Only 15-20% of the Rs 220 crore capex has been spent.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand or realisation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations were higher on average in Q1 but are now falling with oil. Domestic demand is strong across sectors; exports are the main issue, mainly MENA.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz; management says volumes fall when exports are disrupted.
Q1 margins were lifted by inventory gains and supply tightness; management said the next 3-4 months will show whether margins hold.

Nitrile latex overcapacity in the glove supply chain and possible Asian expansions, including Malaysia (starting July-August 2026).
Working capital and inventory values rise with raw material prices; net cash has fallen.
Q2 seasonality: rains affect construction and footwear demand (the June-August quarter).

523694|2026-09.headline: Apcotex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 48% YoY to Rs 499 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 11.69% as gross margins compressed.

EBITDA margin was 11.69% versus 12.06% a year earlier, and PAT margin was 6.98%. H1 FY27 was the company's strongest half-year, with revenue of Rs 1,025 crore (+44%), EBITDA of Rs 175 crore (+121%, margin 17.12%) and PAT of Rs 114 crore (+156%). Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses, and more aggressive pricing to win export volumes.

segments.name: Nitrile latex
segments.commentary: Running close to full capacity; management said Q1 margins were a blip and Q2 normalised but remain much better than the last three years. Further expansion decision deferred pending a couple more quarters of margin data.

segments.name: NBR (solid nitrile butadiene rubber)
segments.commentary: Sole Indian producer, entirely import-dependent; plant has run at full capacity for about 1.5 to 2 years. Capex project targeted for commissioning around April 2027. H1 NBR margin said to be slightly higher than synthetic latex.

segments.name: Synthetic latex (SBR)
segments.commentary: Serves about five industries; construction strongest, paper and textiles decent, tyres okay, carpets a laggard due to MENA dependence. SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next year.

guidance_outlook: Management targets a long-run volume CAGR of about 10% (20-30% above GDP growth) over the next three to five years, with construction faster and carpet slower.
Management aims for EBITDA margin closer to 15% but is comfortable with about 12% given high raw material costs; focus is on volumes, EBITDA per ton and ROCE.
Part of the Q1 inventory losses should reverse as prices rose again in October-November due to oil; Q3 is only one month old, so outcome uncertain.
NBR capacity expected to commission around April 2027, with utilisation ramping over two to three years.
Remaining capex outflow of about Rs 155 crore (of Rs 220 crore total, about Rs 65 crore spent) to be spent through next year and beyond; SBR may slip into a later quarter.
capex_capacity: Valia expansion capex of Rs 210 crore (later referenced as Rs 220 crore) largely on track; about Rs 65 crore spent, about Rs 155 crore remaining.
NBR (solid) plant targeted for commissioning around April 2027; SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next fiscal year.
Nitrile latex expansion undecided; most engineering ready, requiring only added reactors; board did not decide at its 28 October meeting.

Company does not disclose segment-wise volumes.
demand_pricing: Export volumes recovered in Q2 after a decline in Q1; shipping to Saudi Arabia (West Coast) and Fujairah improved versus Q1, though MENA remains tight.
Management said it was more aggressive on pricing to win orders in other markets, which lowered gross margin; EBITDA per ton was higher YoY.
Competitor shutdowns in Q1 benefited the company, which kept plants running; overcapacity in nitrile latex persists from COVID-era additions.
Carpet volumes hit by US tariffs, the war and high ocean freight; management said Q2 carpet volumes were broadly flat YoY.
Paper overcapacity increasing, though final paper demand is okay; construction is the strongest segment.
India accounts for 65-67% of sales; Q2 seasonally weak due to monsoon-related demand dip.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins at a four-quarter low, and what drove the rise in export volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses in the quarter, and more aggressive pricing. Exports improved with better ship availability to Saudi Arabia and Fujairah, plus orders from other markets. EBITDA per ton and ROCE were better YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the nitrile latex cycle and does oversupply persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Running close to full capacity; Q2 margins normalised from a strong Q1 but are much better than the last three years. Overcapacity from COVID-era additions remains even after some smaller and older plants shut. Expansion decision deferred for a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a timeline and funding breakup for the Rs 210 crore expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: NBR commissioning targeted for about April 2027, with two to three years to full utilisation. Management said about Rs 65 crore is spent and Rs 155 crore remains, but did not give a debt versus internal accrual split in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Which synthetic latex industries are growing or lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction (repairs, waterproofing, oil drilling) has grown strongly; paper and textiles are decent and tyres okay. Carpets are the laggard due to MENA and Western market exposure from tariffs, war and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: What long-term volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 10% average volume CAGR over three to five years, driven by population and GDP growth in India and Southeast Asia, plus substitution of European supply in MENA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential Q2-to-Q3 decline a pattern, and is there a strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the Q1-to-Q2 seasonal decline from monsoon-linked demand. It said it had not analysed Q2-to-Q3 patterns and would review five years of data. It urged investors to focus on annual trends, given oil-linked inventory gains and losses.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin volatility from oil-linked raw material prices and inventory gains or losses; Q3 pricing recovery depends on the rest of the quarter.
Carpet segment volume weakness from MENA and Western exposure, freight costs and tariffs.
Nitrile latex overcapacity may cap margins; the expansion decision is pending.
NBR commissioning slip beyond April 2027 would delay ramp-up; SBR plant timing may slip to a later quarter.

Anti-dumping on NBR imports was not granted, per management.

rows.label: Export recovery to MENA and other markets

rows.label: Working capital build from higher input costs

523704|2026-03.headline: Mastek Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3.6% QoQ to INR938 crore with EBITDA steady at 16.1%; 12-month backlog up 13.5% YoY in USD.
523704|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as a stable quarter: USD revenue of $103.5 million was up 1.4% QoQ (flat in constant currency), and EBITDA held at 16.1% despite a $1.1 million salary increase. FY26 revenue grew 7% YoY in INR to INR3,699 crore, with EBITDA flat at 15.8%. Reported PAT was hit by a INR23.7 crore exceptional Labour Code true-up in Q4 (INR6.4 crore in Q3), which management moved below EBITDA and which restated Q3 EBITDA to 16.8%. Management guided to FY27 growth above FY26 but declined to give a numerical target.

segments.commentary: Described as the star of the quarter; ramp-up from large North American BFSI wins and UK/AMEA FS orders. Management said FCA deal reached 60+ onsite resources and will be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Sequential dip in Q4 from project timing gaps (live transitions in UK and US) with new projects yet to start; management expects recovery as new programmes ramp.

Effective tax rate expected at 24.5% to 24.7% in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY26 low growth be followed by a stronger first half of FY27, and will management give a growth number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 would be a growth year with better performance than FY26 but declined to give a numerical guidance, citing an unstable macro and AI-led pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the average effective tax rate would be 24.5% to 24.7%; the Q4 rate was lower because of a past-year assessment provision reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in AMEA from deferred WAR revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about $0.5 million of WAR revenue deferred from Q2 was recognised in Q4; new AMEA decision-making has slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US and AMEA margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: North America saw pressure from revenue stabilisation and the wage hike; AMEA had flat revenue and the wage hike, with the full wage-hike impact in Q4 and not carrying into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-led deal ramp and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-led deals are in two categories: AI-led technology deals (legacy modernisation, AI testing, managed services) and early AI use-case deployments; margins are in line with current gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company use its growing cash?
qa_highlights.answer: M&A will focus on domain and vertical capabilities rather than digital periphery, with smaller AI investments and larger partnerships with AI players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the headcount and utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount growth is expected to be slower than revenue growth, so revenue per resource should improve; utilisation was 80% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 73 days sustainable, and what is the fixed-price share?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects DSO to stay in a stable range near 73 days over the long term, with short-term variation of a few days; about 40% of the business is fixed-price, and North America is above 50-55%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up timing for the ATLAS, FCA and Biometric deals?
qa_highlights.answer: FCA is ramping with more than 60 onsite resources and should be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27; ATLAS and Biometric are renewals with expanded scope, with ramp-up expected between Q1 and Q2 FY27.

The FCA deal has already started ramping up.
The renewals clearly are being extremely price competitive.
So we definitely have a stronger foundation as we enter into FY27.

523704|2026-06.headline: Mastek Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR 985 crore (1.8% cc), with 12-month backlog up 25% YoY to $310 million.
523704|2026-06.overview: Revenue was $104.8 million, up 1.2% QoQ, with 15.4% operating EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 105.9 crore. Middle East disruption raised bench costs and delayed collections, weighing on margin, while UK and North America both grew sequentially. Management highlighted a $25 million, five-year AI transformation deal in North America and a 12-month backlog of $310 million. Top-5 and top-10 client revenue declined QoQ due to a timing gap on NHS England projects, and ESOP expense starts from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: +3.2% QoQ; +13.3% YoY in USD; +25% YoY in INR
After paying INR 107 crore variable pay

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Grew 3% QoQ in constant currency; EBIT near 20%. BFSI growth driven by FCA ramp-up, healthcare had a transition with NHS England old projects closing before new data modernization projects started.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew about 2% QoQ in constant currency and 6% in INR; backlog up 29.8% QoQ and 23.5% YoY. Large $25 million Salesforce Agentforce AI deal expected to ramp by H2 FY27.

segments.name: Middle East (AMEA)
segments.commentary: Faced severe headwinds from West Asia crisis, raising bench cost and delaying collections; some new orders signed late in quarter, but predictability low and ramp-up uncertain.

UK healthcare expected to ramp back from Q2 and H2; North America expected to become a growth engine by H2 FY27.
Middle East expected to stay flat at least, with return to growth if geopolitical stability improves.

North America to reach $28 million to $30 million quarterly run-rate before delivering mid-teens margins.
capex_capacity: North America needs scale of $28 million to $30 million quarterly revenue to deliver mid-teens margins; company is investing in sales and marketing there and plans further investment in healthcare and life sciences.
Headcount rose by 167 to 4,897 in Q1, with UK adding 125 on new project ramp-ups.

Internal business transformation: core systems (CRM, recruitment, payables) replaced with AI-native solutions; resources shifting to forward deployed engineers and forward deployed domain consultants, with a large portion of resources to become FDEs/FDDCs.
demand_pricing: 12-month backlog $310 million, up 3.2% QoQ; management said total order book (TCV) trends are also improving but does not disclose order book numbers.

40-plus AI-led new opportunities closed in Q1; large-deal pipeline increased across geographies; AI deals come from existing accounts (maturity model Level 0 to 5) and net new accounts linked to Oracle, Salesforce, Snowflake and Databricks.
Aggressive price competition on new wins and renewals; discounts generally around 15%, reaching 20-25% in one or two cases, not 50%.
Incumbent challenges on existing accounts and champion-challenger wins in new accounts are the key competitive headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: When will the FCA, Atlas and HADES deals and the US deal ramp up? Why did top-5 client revenue fall 4% QoQ and 12% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: FCA has started ramping and will ramp more in Q2; HADES is a renewal with steady revenue, not incremental; the North America deal ramps by H2 FY27. Top-client decline is a one-time timing gap as NHS England old projects closed before new data modernization projects began.

qa_highlights.question: How have TCV trends been, are discounts becoming irrational, and will healthcare return to sequential growth from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: TCV is moving in the right direction; the $25 million 5-year deal is an example. Discounts are around 15%, up to 20-25% in one or two cases, not 50%. UK healthcare expected to ramp from Q2 and into H2; US healthcare to ramp by H2, not firm for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Excluding the $25 million US deal, the order book looks flat QoQ; how does the funnel look, when will Middle East deals ramp, and will US and Middle East margins stay suppressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Large-deal pipeline has grown across geographies. Middle East healthcare deal closed in Q1 with more close to signature; Middle East expected to stay flat at least. Margin pressure came from slower-than-expected ramp-ups causing bench cost and one-time collection slowdowns, expected to reverse later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting cost trend and ESOP impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Subcontracting at 18.5% of revenue, in line with Q4. ESOP grant from Q2 with an impact of $400,000 to $500,000 per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What changed between Q4 and Q1 to make commentary more positive, and what was the EBITDA margin bridge Q4 to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trajectory is similar to Q4, with more AI demand and execution of backlog from the last 3 to 4 quarters. Margin change reflected Middle East provisions for doubtful debts and unbilled amounts, mix change and UK regulatory costs, offset by cost efficiency and currency tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state EBITDA and EBIT margin given ESOP costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given; Q2 margin will be impacted by ESOP and increments; full-year impact to be mitigated significantly through internal cost efficiencies.

UK public sector budget and policy changes after political leadership change.
North America ramp-down of legacy projects must be offset before H2 turnaround.
Competitive pricing pressure and AI-led incumbent challenges on existing accounts.
Income tax assessment FY2022-23: INR 91 crore transfer pricing and INR 32.5 crore domestic income added; estimated tax impact about INR 31 crore; appeal filed 26 June.
DSO rose to 75 days; ESOP and Q2 increment costs will pressure margins.

523704|2026-09.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.
523704|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ in constant currency to $107.3M (Rs 1,018.7 crore, up 8.3% YoY in INR), with PAT of Rs 105.7 crore. Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

financial_highlights.change: -7.7% QoQ, +2.3% YoY in USD, +10.4% YoY in INR

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: up about Rs 36 crore after Rs 50 crore dividend and Rs 55 crore loan repayment

segments.name: UK-Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4.1% in the quarter, and UK EBIT was 18%. Financial Services grew over 16% QoQ, and public sector grew 6.1% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences lagged on right-shifted starts, and several public-sector orders were put on hold pending the new government's budget.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Total backlog rose 7.8% QoQ and 47.9% YoY. Management expects a meaningful growth turnaround from H2, though a $25M federal deal start has slipped to after the mid-term elections.

segments.name: APAC & Middle East
segments.commentary: Some older contracts were signed, giving a revenue bounce-back in Q2. Management said the Middle East outlook is uncertain and performance is well below plan, especially in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Public sector grew 6.1% QoQ and Financial Services grew 15.3% QoQ. Healthcare & Life Sciences has been slow for two quarters, with management expecting recovery after beta-phase contract awards in Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: Margin target: improve EBITDA by at least 160 bps in the medium term, with the return to the 16% mark dependent on macro and geopolitical factors.
US and Middle East margins expected to improve from Q3, which should offset some of the UK mix-driven margin loss.
FY27 expected to beat FY26, with H2 seen as no slower than H1, though management flagged Middle East and geopolitical risk.
North America expected to see a meaningful growth turnaround from H2.
A UK NHS-related data transformation contract (north of GBP 100M) is an H2 event and would be incremental to TCV; a bridge contract covers about six months.
Subcontracting expected to stay around 18-20% of revenue, moving by about one percentage point in the short term.
Revenue and AI metrics, plus a Data & AI horizontal split, to be disclosed from next quarter (Q3 FY27).
capex_capacity: Headcount closed at 4,810, down 87 QoQ due to workforce restructuring and a change in onsite/offshore mix.
Utilisation including trainees fell 0.8% QoQ, reflecting investment in domain resources.
Sale of Chennai property completed, booked as an exceptional gain, offset by restructuring costs and a write-off of old receivables (one-time).
Attrition (LTM) fell to 15.2% from 16.4%, the second consecutive quarterly decline.
Added 18 new customers in the quarter versus 13 in Q1.
demand_pricing: AI deals made up more than 40% of deals won in the quarter, and about 45% of the total order book. 53 AI deals were closed.
AI transformation deals run at roughly $0.5M to $5M each. AI productivity takeout deals can be much larger, with a $10M+ North America life sciences win.
AI transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, sometimes above 50%. AI productivity deals are price-aggressive with compressed margins.
Project business rose to 44-45% of revenue from about 40%, mostly fixed-bid. UK public sector and healthcare buy on rate cards.
Average deal tenure is about 3 years plus 2 years in UK-Europe and 18-24 months in North America.
Pipeline includes $100M+ deals to be adjudicated over 6-9 months.
Healthcare softness in UK-Europe is tied to the alpha-to-beta recontracting gap and a ramp-down in an offshore UK healthcare account.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book weakness execution-led or UK pressure? Is FY27 still expected to beat FY26? What is the ramp on new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: A $25M US federal deal start was delayed until after the mid-term elections, and a UK contract is consuming more slowly than planned, with pickup expected around Q4. Management still expects FY27 to beat FY26, citing H2 strength in UK and US and a Middle East dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI deals from new or existing clients, what are the deal sizes, and when will AI revenue be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI deals come from both new and existing clients, with at least two net-new wins in the examples shown. Typical AI deal size is $0.5M-$5M, and AI revenue figures will be presented from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline, and what is the bridge to the 160 bps recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments and ESOPs cost 190 bps. A UK mix shift from high-margin projects to lower-margin sovereignty and security-cleared work cost about 200 bps. AI-led efficiencies and restructuring recovered about 200 bps. Forex was a 20 bps tailwind. US and Middle East margins are expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America growth muted, and how do BFSI and healthcare trends differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a North America turnaround from H2. Healthcare & Life Sciences remains its strongest vertical, and BFSI growth is mainly UK-led. North America financial services is still early-stage.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI deals grow after the initial POC, and what margins do they earn?

524091|2026-03.headline: Carysil Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 16% to INR237 crores and PAT (after MI) jumped 42% to INR27 crores, with EBITDA margin at 20.3%.

524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.
524164|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR756 crore against INR551 crore a year earlier, up 37%. EBITDA rose 60.7% to INR111 crore, lifting margin to 14.6% from 12.4%, and PAT grew 89.9% to INR64.5 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher capacity utilisation, product mix, export realisations and operational efficiencies, and said there was no material inventory gain in the quarter. FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 36% in Q1 FY26; non-ibu revenue up 67% YoY
Management did not split volume vs price

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (API)
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen products were 43% of pharma revenue, up 67% YoY; growth described as broad-based across the portfolio. Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, with paracetamol lower at about 55% of enhanced 10,800 MTPA capacity.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said the chemical segment margin trended up in the quarter, helped by higher ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride capacity, better realisations and higher exports. Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production only in May 2026, with steady-state revenue potential of about INR120 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth of 15-20% (management said around 20% in Q&A), EBITDA margin 14-15%, exports about 25-30% of revenue.
Management said the INR2,600-2,700 crore full-year revenue guidance remains unchanged, may be crossed in the current scenario, but will not be upgraded.
FY28 (indicative, conditional on current scenario): revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 15-17%.
Near term: non-ibuprofen to reach about 50% of pharma revenue, with roughly 50% ibuprofen; by FY29, non-ibu expected at 50-55% of API segment with margins similar to ibuprofen.
Capex of about INR200 crore a year; about 60% expansion and new products, 40% infrastructure and efficiency. Next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27.
Regulatory: two to three more quarters expected for Triacetin approvals.
capex_capacity: Paracetamol capacity tripled from 3,600 MTPA to 10,800 MTPA; operating at about 55%, targeted near 70% by end FY27.
Triacetin plant of 6,000 MTPA commenced production in May 2026; capacity to ramp as market penetration grows. Inputs are acetic acid and glycerol.
Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.
Capex of around INR200 crore per year, with INR100-200 crore spent annually over the last four to five years.
R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.
524164|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the diversification story, but guarded on forward numbers: management held guidance, declined to upgrade it, and said FY28 targets depend on current conditions. It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a strong note, with healthy demand across key products, improved capacity utilization, favorable product mix, and continued focus on operational efficiency.
Our objective is not merely to add capacities, but to build meaningful and sustainable positions across a diversified API portfolio.
So the guidance will be remaining in the same line. However, we will be able to -- having the current scenario, we think that we may cross that number. But we don't want to upgrade the guidance
Abhay Raj Singh: Maulik ji, this is on the basis of the current scenario. Suppose down the line in next six-month scenario got changed, then what we are saying may not be possible.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Paracetamol tripled to 10,800 MTPA but running at ~55% and targeted ~70% by end FY27; Triacetin 6,000 MTPA only began May 2026 with approvals 2-3 quarters away, and no major new project expected to commission in FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management said the majority of the ~42-43% pharma growth came from volumes, most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, paracetamol is ramping from ~55% toward ~70%, and FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% (around 20% in Q&A) is held.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation (group ~82.5%), but management reiterated a steady ~INR200 crore a year capex and said the next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27, so a large new announcement is not guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue grew 37% YoY and management said FY27 revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range, but it explicitly declined to upgrade guidance, which was held at 15-20% growth and 14-15% EBITDA margin.

rows.why: FY28 margin outlook (15-17%) is explicitly conditional on the current scenario, and raw-material/energy volatility from the US-Iran conflict could compress the 14-15% FY27 margin if pass-through lags; sequential gross margin already fell in the quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Non-ibuprofen share of pharma revenue rose to 43% (from 36%) and is guided to ~50% near term, with two to three more US FDA ANDA approvals pending and Triacetin approvals expected in two to three quarters.

rows.label: Triacetin and ANDA approvals
rows.why: Management expects two to three more quarters for Triacetin approvals and two to three more US FDA ANDA-linked approvals are pending, with CEP approval already for all products and US FDA approval for five.

rows.label: Raw material spread and pass-through
rows.why: Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices spiked in March 2026 and are now stable to slightly easing, and management expects the spread to hold, but some prices were pre-agreed with large customers and sequential gross margin fell in Q1.

rows.label: Export share normalisation
rows.why: Export share rose to 28.5% from 24.4%, but agreed customer quantities mean it can move quarter to quarter and could fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 37% revenue growth and diversification into non-ibuprofen products, but held guidance without upgrading and made FY28 margins conditional on current conditions; it was evasive on the volume/price split and export mix, which analysts pushed on.

524164|2026-09.headline: IOL Chemicals Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to INR795 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4%, with PAT of INR65 crore (up ~117%).
524164|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR795 crore, up about 40% YoY, with H1 revenue of INR1,551 crore (up about 39%). EBITDA rose about 80% YoY to INR115 crore, a 14.4% margin (up 321 bps), and PAT more than doubled in H1 to about INR130 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to 25%+ (revised up from 15-20%) and EBITDA margin of 14-15%, and said prices of key products have been stable for 2-3 quarters. Three projects worth about INR500 crore were announced, to be funded from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR64 crore, 11.2% margin in Q2 FY26; +321 bps
~70% YoY vs 11.8% margin in H1 FY26
vs INR30 crore in Q2 FY26, ~117% growth
vs INR64 crore in H1 FY26, more than doubled
vs 38% in Q2 FY26; ~70% YoY growth in non-ibuprofen revenue

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen API portfolio grew ~70% YoY in Q2 and reached 45% of pharma revenue (38% a year ago). Ibuprofen remains an important line, with capacity expansion from 12,000 to 18,000 MTPA planned.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Chemicals EBIT contribution rose to ~7% in Q2 from ~1% a year ago, on better realisations, operating efficiencies and procurement. Ethyl Acetate capacity was raised from 1 lakh to 1.2 lakh tonnes; Acetic Anhydride and Ethyl Acetate ran at full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25%+ YoY, revised up from earlier 15-20%; management expects H2 performance similar to H1.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%; long-term sustainable company-wide EBITDA margin of 15-17% cited for FY29 targeting.
Ibuprofen expansion (12,000 to 18,000 MTPA) targeted for commissioning in FY28, with meaningful benefit expected only in FY28-29.
CDMO formulation and specialty chemicals projects expected to commence commercial operations in FY27 per the opening remarks; later clarified as commercialisation in FY28 for CDMO.
Capex planned at INR250 crore for FY27, about half spent in H1. Management said no further borrowing is planned, with the INR200 crore working capital line as the peak requirement.
Management expects other expenses (power, fuel, freight) to ease in Q3 and Q4, with freight cost to be passed on to customers.
capex_capacity: Three projects announced in Q2 totalling about INR500 crore, funded from internal accruals: ibuprofen expansion (12,000 to 18,000 MTPA, backward integrated, FY28), formulation CDMO (1,500 million tablets per year, Europe-focused, FY28 commercialisation), and a dedicated specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing plant (plant nearly commissioned, first batches expected in November 2026).
FY27 capex planned at INR250 crore, with roughly half spent in H1 FY27.

Ibuprofen and major products run at 90-100% capacity utilisation over the last 3-4 quarters. Paracetamol capacity is about 10,800 MT, with a plan to optimise to 100% first. A paracetamol facility of 18,000 MT was mentioned in a question.
Ethyl Acetate capacity raised from 1 lakh to 1.2 lakh tonnes through debottlenecking, not a new plant.
demand_pricing: Ibuprofen prices have been stable for the last 2-3 quarters. Management expects them to hold at similar levels for the next 1-2 quarters and declined to forecast 2-3 year prices.

API customer onboarding takes about 6-8 months to start commercial orders.
CDMO: development is under way with 2-3 customers, mainly European, with existing customers; validation takes about a year including customer approval.

qa_highlights.question: Ibuprofen realisation trends and whether the company will benefit in Q3/Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices have been stable for several quarters and are expected to stay flat for 1-2 quarters; the price benefit is already in the P&L, and the new capacity is a strategic move rather than a response to current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will incremental ibuprofen capacity go to merchant or formulation customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is roughly 50:50 between new customers and internal CDMO consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and borrowing needs for the rest of FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR200 crore working capital line as of 30 September 2026 is the peak requirement, that no further borrowing is planned, and that cash flow and cash on hand are sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 25% growth imply lower H2 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said 25%+ is for the full year on value basis, with H2 expected to perform at a similar level to H1.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and margins are expected in CDMO and the overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turn is about 1:3 for chemicals, 1:1 for API and 1:1 to 1:1.25 for CDMO, around 1:1.75 blended. CDMO margins are expected to exceed API margins, but management said it was too early to quantify them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: A renowned global chemical company customer under a cost-plus, long-term tolling arrangement with a dedicated plant; the product is confidential and is not sold in the open market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about 14.5% of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to higher power and fuel costs in the summer quarter and higher freight cost, and expects these to decline in Q3 and Q4.

Raw material price volatility and acetic acid spikes; pass-through clauses in contracts are not fully in place. Management could not quantify the ibuprofen price trend beyond 1-2 quarters.
Other expenses rose to about 14.5% of sales (vs 13.7-14% historically); watch whether freight and power costs ease in Q3 and Q4.

Triacetin export commercial orders have not yet started despite REACH registration.

rows.why: Management said no further borrowing is planned and cash flow plus cash on hand are sufficient, with INR250 crore FY27 capex about half spent in H1.

524200|2026-03.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-level volume growth guided at about 15%.
ATBS volume growth of about 15% YoY expected for at least the next three years.
FY27 capex earmarked at INR200-250 crores (about INR200 crores at Vinati Organics and INR40-50 crores at VOPL); management says about INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years.
AO and butyl phenol revenue targeted at INR800-900 crores in the next two years.
Long-term EBITDA margin of 26-27% considered achievable, given expansions, new products and raw material swings.
Gross block addition of about INR500 crores assumed at 1:1 asset turn.
Two to three new downstream products expected in H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28.
Company will continue to fund expansion from internal accruals and remain debt-free.

ATBS: a Phase 1 of 10,000 tonnes is commissioned. Total ATBS capacity is about 50,000 tonnes for lower molecular weight grades and about 40,000 tonnes for higher purity grades. Phase 2 (another 10,000 tonnes) expected by October 2026. Two-phase cost about INR250-300 crores.
CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Pipeline products are downstream derivatives of MEHQ, butyl phenols and antioxidants, plus TAA, PTAP and 4-MAP at VOPL. Isoamylene derivatives were dropped. Monomers and polymers are under consideration but not confirmed.
Butyl phenol capacity of about 50,000 tonnes is at 70-75% utilisation with no space to expand.
demand_pricing: Demand softened from October 2025. Management says demand has since recovered, and ATBS is still growing at double-digit rates industry-wide.

AO faces undercutting and aggressive selling by Chinese producers. Management says ADD was not granted and has been reapplied, and it notes that 80-90% of ADD applications were rejected in the sector.

qa_highlights.question: What new products are in the pipeline, and when will they come online?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?
qa_highlights.answer: ATBS is about one-third and AO is 15-20%. IB is 10-12%, IBB is 10-12%, and customised and other products make up the rest, with overall ATBS and AO together around 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26. Management expects about INR100-120 crores in FY27 once reengineering finishes, with revenue from Q2/Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40-50 crores of the FY27 capex goes to VOPL and about INR200 crores to the parent. VOPL CWIP of about INR120-125 crores is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AO growth lagged, and what is the status of the ADD?
qa_highlights.answer: AO growth was about 5% in FY26 because of aggressive Chinese undercutting. ADD was not granted, has been reapplied, and a decision could take 6-9 months.

risks_watch: AO margins and volumes depend on the anti-dumping duty decision, which could take another 6-9 months after reapplication, while Chinese players undercut prices.
VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on finishing process reengineering by September 2026. The plant had teething troubles with its new process.
ATBS Phase 2 utilisation is expected to build mainly in FY28, and the plant is running at about 75-80% utilisation.
Butyl phenol capacity is at 70-75% utilisation with no room to expand, so growth may cut merchant sales.
Sector cyclicality has shortened, with sharp swings in raw material prices, logistics and customer destocking.
Management guidance rests on about 15% volume growth, a recovery from the October 2025 slowdown and IBB volumes resuming after the Iran war disruption.
