524208|2026-03.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
524208|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Energy applications
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; volumes down 4% QoQ on lower Middle East exports. Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to commission soon. Middle East is about 9-10% of company revenue, mostly energy.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Steady volume growth but margin pressure continues. A new $150 million multiyear agro intermediate contract runs to March 2030 with no incremental capex.

segments.name: Polymers
segments.commentary: Strong growth phase on EV-linked demand; MPDA continues to underperform due to Chinese competition.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints
segments.commentary: Share of revenue about 10-11%. Demand pressure in 3,3'-DCBH globally, partly offset by domestic demand; some low-margin demand destruction possible in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Stable in the quarter; PNCB chain expected to benefit from China anti-involution from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (about INR 150 crore a year is maintenance), funding Zone IV completion and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract.
Zone IV: calcium chloride and multipurpose plant to be commercialised within the quarter; remaining blocks commissioned through FY27 after a 3-4 month delay; initial revenue from Q2 FY27.
Management aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite higher working capital, as capex intensity falls and cash flow improves.
Tax rate guided at about 9-15% going forward.
Working capital target of 55-60 days, with the company currently above this level.
Augene (Superform JV) to commission around June-July 2026; recycling JV to commission in CY26.
Interest-cost and EBITDA potential from Zone IV and the UPL JV unchanged at INR 300-450 crore, but realisation may slip 6-7 months.
capex_capacity: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore; gross block expected at INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27.
Energy expansion to 360 KTPA on track for commissioning soon.
Contract labour availability in the capex region down 35%, delaying last-mile pipeline work.
Augene JV and recycling JV commissioning in 2026; DCB debottlenecking under way.
About 50% of the Bayer/Dicamba-linked asset is used for one intermediate, with steady volumes.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60% in the quarter; some more than doubled.
Agro pricing is up sharply from January, but the company is holding spreads rather than absolute prices; full pass-through expected over 3-6 months.
NCB margins and pricing improved on China's anti-involution policy; DCB remains robust on EV demand.
MMA economics are volatile with gasoline-naphtha cracks ranging from negative to up $20/bbl; Middle East shipments physically halted, US shipments steady, Europe starting.
Physical supply of methanol (about a couple of months' cover) and sulfur (a few weeks' cover) is secure.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q4 margins, especially in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Zone IV EBITDA and the net debt/EBITDA target at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost and operating-leverage initiatives are on track; the EBITDA potential is unchanged but may slip 6-7 months. Net debt/EBITDA was about 3.6x at year-end.

risks_watch: Middle East flows halted for 6-8 weeks; full Q1 FY27 impact on energy volumes depends on West Asia stabilisation.
Working capital and net debt rise if crude moves to USD 140-150/bbl.
Zone IV labour shortage and 3-4 month delay; check commissioning and first revenue in Q2 FY27.
Potential demand destruction in low-margin dyes and pigments over 3-6 months.
Unhedged USD 87 million FX loan; further rupee depreciation would add revaluation losses.
MPDA and agro margins remain under pressure from Chinese competition.

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

Zone IV commissioning is delayed 3-6 months; the MPP is expected to produce first product in August 2026 and commissioning will be announced thereafter. Management expects 5-10 products in FY27 and 25-30 by FY28.
Sabic-linked backward-integration project commissioning expected around Sep-Oct 2027.
capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.
Zone IV: 97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete across the five chemistry blocks; full manpower restored, with commissioning expected in FY27 and ramp-up over FY28-FY29.
PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.
NCB chain debottlenecking is being evaluated within existing assets given demand in India.
Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inflation (benzene, sulphur, methanol, aniline) was passed through to customers; high prices reduced purchasing power in dyes, selected agro and polymer compounds.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.
Exports were 59% of revenue; US-bound DAP shipments carry 2-3 month voyage times that delay revenue recognition.
China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.
Non-energy volumes fell on delayed purchasing in a high-price environment, with some supply-chain effects; management said Middle East exposure in non-energy is low.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

risks_watch: Zone IV: five chemistry blocks face a 3-6 month delay and slower ramp-up; the MPP first product is expected in August 2026, and the FY28 Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance (which includes Augene) depends on this ramp-up.

Earnings quality: management said FX and inventory gains (Rs 50-60 crore, roughly Rs 47 crore per an analyst's figure) helped Q1, and it declined to commit to a forward quarterly EBITDA run rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly price swings.

Energy seasonality and West Asia: management expects winter weakness from late October to December, and West Asia volumes (share down to about 2% from about 15%) are not yet restored; utilisation of the 360 KTPA fuel additives capacity is the key test over the next 12 months.
Working capital and leverage: management said working capital expanded and debt and finance costs rose in Q1; watch debt levels as imported-raw-material inventory (1-1.5 months) carries price risk.

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.

I would again hesitate to hazard a guess.
So we did not see the EBITDA run rate can be maintained.
The actual sales numbers is something that we have removed from the slides because they was getting utilized in a situation which was not favourable for the company.

524208|2026-09.headline: Aarti Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73% YoY to Rs 3,887 crore and EBITDA hit a record Rs 418 crore (+44% YoY), helped by raw-material pass-through.
524208|2026-09.overview: Aarti Industries reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA for Q2 FY27, with H1 EBITDA above Rs 802 crore against Rs 507 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by volumes and by passing through higher raw-material costs, with Energy-linked products the main contributor. Net debt rose above Rs 4,650 crore on working capital and finance costs, prompting a Rs 1,000 crore fund-raise enabling resolution approved by shareholders on 31 October 2026. Zone IV Phase I was commissioned on 7 September 2026, with most of the Rs 1,800-1,900 crore CWIP expected to be capitalised by 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.

Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.

524348|2026-06.headline: Aarti Drugs Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA margin hit 13.8%, driven mainly by API price hikes.
524348|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA rose 30% to INR96.9 crore, with margin up 120 bps to 13.8%. PAT fell to INR50.1 crore from INR54.0 crore, but the prior year included a INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund PAT growth is stated at 29%. Management said API price increases tied to West Asia conflict and raw material volatility drove most growth, while volume grew about 3.5%. Sayakha utilisation rose above 60% for the first time, and the USFDA API block and Baddi formulation expansion are progressing.

financial_highlights.change: +35% YoY (vs INR51.1 crore); PBT margin 9.9%, +120 bps
vs INR54.0 crore in Q1 FY26, which included INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund growth 29%
+20% YoY (vs INR521.3 crore); about 89% of consolidated
+149% YoY (as stated by analyst; management confirmed)

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Antibiotic 35.0%, antidiabetic 18.2%, antiprotozoal 18.5%, anti-inflammatory 11.9%, antifungal 10.2% and others 6.1% of API sales. Metformin prices are up about 20% versus pre-war levels, though below the March-April peak.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.6 crore, up 8% YoY, with about 74% from exports. Baddi brownfield expansion is expected to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR82 crore, up 149% YoY, driven by the Sayakha plant. Methylamine ran at about 64-65% utilisation (about 60 tonnes/day, about 3,500 tonnes in the quarter).

segments.name: Salicylic acid (Tarapur)
segments.commentary: Only 67 tonnes produced in the quarter, as production was kept low. Derivatives plant (methyl salicylate, 350-400 tpm capacity) has started trials at 5-10 tonnes. Anti-dumping duty is expected in about one year.

guidance_outlook: Management says 14% EBITDA margin is achievable and 15% should be easy once the greenfield plants reach higher utilisation; a further 200 bps gain depends on prices normalising.
Volume growth of 10-15% over the next two years is seen as achievable, and about 10% even if the salicylic acid derivatives do not pick up.
Volume growth in the remaining three quarters is expected to be better than June quarter, as demand recovers once prices stabilise.
Specialty Chemicals run-rate of Q1 is expected to repeat in the next three quarters and improve further.
Captive consumption from Sayakha is expected to reach 80-90% by December quarter, adding about 1% to gross contribution at peak utilisation.
Metformin capacity to rise from 1,400 to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA-compliant capacity taking about 10-12 months.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 greenfield assets (Sayakha, Tarapur) cost about INR600 crore and are expected to yield about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield projects are expected at 3-4x.
Sayakha plant utilisation was about 65% in Q1 FY27 (versus 30% in Dec-quarter and 40% in Mar-quarter, per management), with about 50% of capacity used captively for antidiabetic intermediates.
Metformin: 1,400 tpm capacity at mid-80s% utilisation; plan to scale to about 2,200 tpm, with the USFDA block (500-550 tpm) being built at Sarigam, which takes 10-12 months. US DMF already filed.

USFDA API plant (E-22): 2 main lines and 1 small line, around 4-5 active products, mostly supplied to Europe. A quasi-greenfield expansion adds 3 multipurpose lines of about 10 tpm each, more than doubling capacity.
Salicylic acid capacity about 600 tpm, utilisation about 70% per management. Derivatives plant at Tarapur (350-400 tpm) commissioned, in trial batches.
demand_pricing: Metformin pricing up about 15-20% versus pre-war; the March-April peak was higher, and prices have since eased slightly.
Price increases were tied to raw material and ammonia shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. Formulation customers cut purchases, which hit domestic volumes; export demand was less affected.
Management says Chinese competition is not a concern for its product set, though some pressure exists from select players.
Salicylic acid prices were cut sharply by Chinese players, so derivatives (salicylates) are now more profitable than salicylic acid itself.
Europe is still a small, under-tapped market for Metformin; EU CEP approvals were obtained for 9 products.

qa_highlights.question: How did metformin realizations move QoQ and YoY, and how will backward integration support market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Harit Shah said metformin prices are up about 15-20% versus pre-war levels. Adhish Patil said the March-April peak was higher and current prices are slightly below it. Metformin capacity is about 1,400 tpm at mid-80s% utilisation, scaling to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When can API supplies to the US market start, given the USFDA block timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: US DMF is already filed. The fresh 500+ tpm block at the same location takes about 10-12 months to build, after which USFDA inspection will be sought with a customer's help. European approval exists for the same facility.

qa_highlights.question: Has the API industry entered a sustained recovery, and what is the asset turn on the INR600 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions remain volatile and it is too early to call. Competition from China is not an issue for its product set, though select players pressure some products. Phase 1 greenfield assets are expected to give about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield about 3-4x, with Sayakha about 50% of capacity used captively.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty Chemicals grew 149% to about INR82 crore: is this sustainable, and what is the methylamine run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhish Patil said the Q1 performance will repeat in the next three quarters and may improve, driven by the Sayakha plant. Methylamine ran at about 64-65% utilisation, roughly 60 tonnes per day or about 3,500 tonnes in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Tarapur salicylic acid plant and the derivatives plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 67 tonnes of salicylic acid were produced in the quarter as output was kept low pending equipment. The derivatives plant (350-400 tpm) has started trial batches of 5-10 tonnes. Anti-dumping duty is delayed by about a year. Chinese price cuts have made salicylates more profitable than salicylic acid.

qa_highlights.question: What were volume and price growth in Q1, and what is the outlook for the remaining three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Aggregate volume grew about 3.5% and price about 16-17% YoY, with most growth from price. Formulation buyers cut stock purchases as prices rose. Volume in the next three quarters is expected to beat the June quarter once prices stabilise, with export demand less affected.

risks_watch: Price-led growth: volume grew only about 3.5% while price rose 16-17%; management expects prices to ease as the West Asia conflict and raw-material shortages resolve, which could reduce realisations and margins.

Margin sustainability: management said 14% EBITDA margin is achievable and 15% should be easy after utilisation rises, but 200 bps further gain depends on price normalisation; Q1 also included write-offs of aged capital WIP.

Sayakha and Tarapur ramp-up: Sayakha utilisation was about 65% in Q1 against the 60-80% target; salicylic acid output of 67 tonnes and anti-dumping duty delayed by about one year keep the Tarapur drag on P&L.
US market entry timing: the USFDA-compliant metformin block (500-550 tpm) takes 10-12 months to build and then needs inspection, so US API supplies are not before about 12 months.
Formulation demand: domestic formulation customers cut purchases at high prices; management expects domestic demand recovery but cited past antibiotic and antidiarrheal demand pressure.
Q1 FY27 PAT declined to INR50.1 crore from INR54.0 crore due to the prior-year tax refund; watch whether reported PAT growth resumes in later quarters.
key_quotes: What is particularly encouraging is that despite this challenging external environment, our op erations remained completely stable throughout the quarter.
So 14% is quite doable. We are almost there.
Yes. So, this first quarter 's performance will definitely repeat for the next 3 quarters.
So achieving 10% to 15% volume growth in next two years should not be a problem.
524348|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and utilisation, with stated targets on margin and volume, but cautious on pricing, saying conditions remain volatile and it is too early to call sustained recovery. Management was evasive on the exact timing of the US API approval and on whether 200 bps of margin gain is achievable.

524370|2026-09.headline: Bodal Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 884 crore (+77% YoY), EBITDA INR 128 crore at 14.4% margin, and net profit INR 81 crore.
524370|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 77% YoY to INR 884 crore, with EBITDA of INR 128 crore (14.4% margin) and net profit of INR 81 crore. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue reached a record INR 1,599 crore (+67%), with EBITDA of INR 203 crore (+114%) and net profit of INR 112 crore versus INR 16 crore in H1 FY26. Management credited higher H acid and vinyl sulphone prices, linked to structural changes in China, and volume growth in dye intermediates. The benzene downstream plant, which had lost about INR 30 crore EBITDA a year, is now ramping up, with utilisation above 85% in October. Management guided to a 12% margin on INR 3,000 crore+ FY27 revenue, but declined to give H acid or vinyl sulphone price data or capacity expansion plans.

segments.name: Dye intermediates
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 345 crore (+88% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 562 crore. H acid and vinyl sulphone are ~35% of this business, with about 40% captively consumed. Management says dye intermediate utilisation is at optimum and no capacity expansion is planned for now.

segments.name: Dyestuff
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 212 crore (+60% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 361 crore. Q2 volume was 5,314 MT versus 3,742 MT in Q1 FY26. Utilisation is about 65-70% on a multi-year average, and management expects realisations to improve in Q3 after a roughly 3-month lag.

segments.name: Basic chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 99 crore (+199% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 183 crore, driven by higher sulphur prices. About 50% of output is captively used in dye intermediates.

segments.name: Chlor-alkali
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 91 crore (+8% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 178 crore (+6%), helped by better realisations. Punjab site has spare land for expansion.

segments.name: Benzene downstream (Saykha)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR 108 crore (Q1 INR 65 crore; Q2 hit by a technical issue). October run-rate was above INR 300 crore, with utilisation around 85%, and management sees INR 350-400 crore annual potential. Management expects it to contribute to net profit from Q3.

segments.name: TCCA
segments.commentary: Roughly break-even at EBITDA. Output rose from about 100 to about 300 tonnes per month after anti-dumping duty. Management plans to double capacity in the next few months using domestically sourced equipment, after Chinese equipment could not be exported.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR 3,000 crore+ is 'very much achievable' and management is targeting about 12% EBITDA margin for the year.
Q3 FY27 expected to show a further top-line and margin increase on the existing order book, and management expects Q4 to be similar to Q2 and Q3, with H2 expected to be better than H1.

Other income of about INR 15 crore expected in H2 from sale of Punjab and Ahmedabad land. Pending Punjab electricity duty subsidy of about INR 50 crore has accrued but is not booked, and about INR 5 crore Gujarat subsidy is yet to be received.
Sustainable tax rate of 25%. Management expects interest cost to fall gradually as term debt is repaid.
FY28: volume growth expected from benzene derivatives, TCCA and dyestuff utilisation. Management says a normalised case could still deliver about INR 2,800 crore revenue and 14-15% EBITDA margin.
capex_capacity: Benzene downstream plant utilisation was about 50% in H1 and above 85% in October, and management expects close to 100% by quarter-end.
Management says it will not expand H acid or dye intermediate capacity for now, and will revisit only if China's structural shift is confirmed, likely after Q4 FY27.
Any brownfield expansion could be commissioned in 1.5-2 years, and a capacity addition could be completed in under 12 months.
Organic and inorganic opportunities of INR 100-200 crore are being considered, with internal projects at Bharuch and the Punjab chlor-alkali site.
TCCA capacity is to be doubled within a few months using domestically procured equipment.
demand_pricing: H acid price peaked near INR 1,800/kg and corrected to about INR 1,600-1,650/kg, which management says is passing through to dyestuff. Management expects it to hold through January.
Vinyl sulphone is at about INR 440-450/kg, with management expecting it to hold for some time. Average realisations were about INR 320/kg in Q1 and INR 360-370/kg in Q2.
H acid average realisation was about INR 600/kg in Q1 and about INR 900/kg in Q2. Management said there is no assessment of the per-kg spread on external H acid sales.
Management says dyestuff prices lag intermediates by about 3 months, so Q3 realisations should improve over Q1 and Q2.
China export trends (H acid, vinyl sulphone, and benzene and dyestuff products) are cited as possible signs of structural change, with no significant new Chinese capacity in recent years.

Aniline is about INR 250/kg and sulphur about INR 90-100/kg, with sulphuric acid falling from about INR 110/kg to about INR 90/kg. Management says about 50% of sulphuric acid output is sold externally.
TCCA prices are about INR 150-160/kg after anti-dumping duty, against INR 110-120/kg before. Management says costs are about INR 160/kg and margins are thin.

qa_highlights.question: Will H acid prices and demand hold after the Chinese festive season, and is there buyer resistance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders are committed through January at about INR 1,600-1,650/kg, and it will reassess in December for February-March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and cash flow from operations weaken in H1 despite higher profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to revenue up 70-80% and higher working capital. He said receivables will stabilise once turnover is steady for one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for cash deployment and debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most free cash will go to repaying term debt, with total debt flat versus March 2026 because working capital rose. It also said it may pursue acquisitions while keeping ratios strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no H acid capacity expansion despite strong demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is already the largest producer, will expand only if the structural shift is confirmed, and that a decision is likely after Q4 FY27. It noted an expansion could be done in under 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCCA outlook after anti-dumping duty, and is there new competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TCCA is near break-even, with capacity rising from 100 to 300 tonnes per month and a plan to double capacity locally. It said new entrants face technical barriers because the plant uses Chinese technology, though some players are evaluating entry.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company's EBITDA margin compare with Kiri Industries, and why is the gap large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dyestuff is a low-margin selling tool for intermediates, benzene derivatives ran at about 50% utilisation in Q2, and TCCA adds little margin. Management said Kiri's EBITDA margin was about 18% versus about 14.5% for the company.

risks_watch: Receivables and working capital are rising with turnover, which is holding back free cash flow and debt reduction.
Price sustainability: H acid, vinyl sulphone and benzene derivative prices depend on China's structural shift and buyer acceptance after China's festive season.
Crude and raw material costs (aniline, sulphur) are elevated, and management expects some top-line correction if crude normalises at $70-80.
Gross margin has been broadly flat at about 40% standalone, so the H acid price rise has not yet lifted gross margin.
Benzene downstream ramp-up and dyestuff realisation improvement in Q3 must come through, and the INR 50 crore Punjab subsidy must be booked.
TCCA capacity expansion and the planned domestic equipment sourcing must deliver margin improvement.
Management has not provided H acid or vinyl sulphone average realisation for Q2 on a precise basis, and the figures given were rough estimates.
524370|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on near-term pricing and margins but conservative on long-term capacity, with management repeatedly declining to commit beyond the next quarter. Specific figures such as H acid and vinyl sulphone realisations were given only as approximate ranges, and some questions were deferred to IR.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 16 crore in H1 FY26

key_quotes: It is very clear that receivable is going to pile up.
We are not looking for anything too big in size because of the pending debt on the book.
Our problem is that our utilization is very less, which we are fixing that problems.

So, anybody wanting to enter this space, it's not going to be easy technically, because our plant was set up by a team of Chinese people, and there is a lot of Chinese technology and equipment's involved in the entire plant.
We are the largest manufacturer with two plants, and we are also the largest manufacturer of another key dye intermediate called vinyl sulphone.

I think this could be structural shift, but I think it is a little bit too soon right now because it's only been a few months, and I think we want to really see how things are in the last quarter of the financial year and then maybe we can decide.

524372|2026-03.headline: Orchid Pharma Q4 FY26 standalone revenue flat YoY at ~INR238 crore with EBITDA ~INR42.3 crore; FY26 EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore.
524372|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR238 crore, broadly flat versus about INR237 crore in Q4 FY25, and EBITDA rose to about INR42.3 crore from about INR40 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue fell to INR811 crore from INR922 crore and EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore, with management attributing this to cephalosporin price erosion and inventory write-downs in Q1 to Q3. Management said gross margins recovered in Q4 and that the worst of the pricing cycle may be behind, while remaining cautious on a full industry recovery. The call also covered the pending Dhanuka Laboratories merger, the 7ACA project, Enmetazobactam out-licensing (no definitive deal signed yet), and a planned US sterile cephalosporin fill-finish push.

segments.name: Base cephalosporin business
segments.commentary: Management is targeting 10-15% growth for FY27 and about 12% EBITDA margin for the base business. Growth is expected mainly from non-regulated markets such as Africa and South Asia.

segments.name: Enmetazobactam (Exblifep)
segments.commentary: Currently sold only in India and Europe; Europe Q1 sales were about 4x the prior quarter but not yet financially meaningful. Lifetime sales guided at $1-2 billion, with peak now expected in year 4-5 after launch.

segments.name: AMS (antimicrobial stewardship)
segments.commentary: Growing steadily and gaining hospital recognition. Currently an EBITDA drag of about INR8 crore a year.

segments.name: Dhanuka Laboratories (pending merger)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR450 crore, down from INR500 crore; EBITDA not yet available as audit is ongoing. Management estimates the merger could add 1-2% to combined EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Base business growth target of 10-15% in FY27, with about 12% EBITDA margin assumed for FY27.
7ACA project commissioning targeted for Q1 CY2027 at Chennai; first sales go internally, third-party sales after first few quarters.
Cefiderocol facility to be commissioned by end CY2026; product launch expected in Q2 or Q3 CY2027, subject to approvals.
Shionogi-linked plant commissioning in December 2026; India launch expected about six months after a clinical trial waiver, i.e. second half CY2027.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing: management hopes to sign at least one deal in the current quarter and about 50% of the identified markets within six months.
Merger with Dhanuka Laboratories: court order reserved in March; written order expected after court vacations.
capex_capacity: Cefiderocol facility: 1 million vial capacity; estimated first-few-years demand about 400,000 vials, with about one-third for India and the rest global; cost-plus agreement with guaranteed fixed PBT.
US sterile fill-finish and formulation capex about INR50 crore, mostly within the Cefiderocol project and largely filing and development expense.

7ACA: about 75% of output to be consumed in-house (25% existing consumption plus downstream intermediates); downstream capacity to be added by reengineering existing plants, with budget set aside; management guided about 5% additional EBITDA from downstream products.

US sterile FDF plan: five to six large sterile products over next few years, addressing about two-thirds of a ~$1.2 billion US cephalosporin opportunity; first ANDAs (Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline) to be filed via a CMO, with Orchid site as second site later.
demand_pricing: Cephalosporin pricing rose in April 2026 on war-related input cost increases (solvents and inputs); management reviews prices almost weekly and is unsure how much cost increases can be passed on.
7ACA price about $61/kg, versus about $55 a couple of quarters ago; long-term average about $60, with a range of $55-65.
Q2 and Q3 FY26 saw inventory bought at high prices sold at lower market prices, causing gross margin pressure; management said Q1 FY26 likely had the largest inventory loss but did not quantify it.
Cefiderocol price cited by analyst at about $150 per vial; management did not confirm the figure.
Enmetazobactam in Europe depends on formulary and government tender inclusion; South Europe inclusion is driving sales growth. Enmetazobactam treated about 30,000 patients in the last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has no Enmetazobactam out-licensing deal been signed despite the earlier one-per-quarter expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said long-term agreements are taking longer than expected; term sheets are signed in some markets and definitive agreements are under negotiation in Japan, Russia, US, Latin America and Southeast Asia. Management hopes for one deal this quarter and expects about 50% of these to be signed within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base business margin and growth outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting about 12% EBITDA margin and 10-15% sales growth in FY27, continuing a four-to-five-year trend. It noted that non-regulated market pricing will stay competitive as capacity expands.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Dhanuka merger a change in 7ACA in-house consumption (75%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said 25% is existing consumption and the rest will be converted into downstream intermediates sold from Orchid Chennai. Only about 20-25% of 7ACA will be sold to third parties; some downstream capacity addition is needed, reengineering existing plants first.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak sales and timing for Enmetazobactam?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime sales are still held at $1-2 billion over the patent life. Peak sales are now expected in the fourth or fifth year after launch rather than the third.

qa_highlights.question: How will Cefiderocol capacity utilisation ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 million vials is sufficient and no near-term expansion is needed. About 400,000 vials are expected in the first few years, depending on geographies opened through GARDP licensing.

qa_highlights.question: Will US ANDAs be filed from a CMO first?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline will be filed through a CMO first to avoid delay from US FDA facility approval, with the Orchid site added later as an alternate manufacturing site.

risks_watch: Pending written order on the Dhanuka Laboratories merger; synergy of 1-2% EBITDA margin depends on completion.
FY26 EBITDA down about 35% YoY; sustainability of Q4 gross margin recovery and price increases amid war-related cost inflation.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing timing: no definitive agreement signed yet; deal flow repeatedly deferred.
7ACA commissioning in Q1 CY2027 described as a race against time; downstream capacity capex still unquantified.
Cefiderocol and US sterile launch timelines depend on regulatory approvals and registrations.
Chinese capacity additions and competitive pricing in non-regulated markets.
524372|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the stabilising pricing backdrop, but cautious on a full industry recovery. Management was evasive on Enmetazobactam deal timing, product-level numbers and the Dhanuka EBITDA, citing confidentiality and audit timing.
key_quotes: While we still remain cautious in calling this a full industry recovery, the business environment currently appears significantly more stable compared to last few quarters.
We now believe the company is entering the next phase, which is platform creation.
So we hope we can continue between 10% to 15% again this year. That's our target.
I would not be able to put a number, but we believe that the first quarter, the loss was the maximum because we were carrying inventory having planned for a good growth during the year.

524394|2026-03.headline: Vimta Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.6% YoY to INR1,120 million, with EBITDA margin of 37.6% and a net debt-free balance sheet.

Management said Q4 was helped by pre-clinical and seasonal food testing, but some expected growth did not materialise, and the company missed its earlier INR500 million annualised run-rate goal. The company entered biologics contract research (biologics and peptides) in FY26, with FY27 framed as a year of execution with no meaningful revenue expected yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said R&D is much smaller in India than in developed markets, and that low-value testing rarely justifies shipping samples overseas.

524394|2026-06.headline: Vimta Labs Q1 FY27 total income rose 13.7% YoY to INR1,129 million, EBITDA margin 36.4%, net debt-free balance sheet.

524394|2026-09.headline: Vimta Q2 FY27 total income up 9.9% YoY to INR1,149 mn, EBITDA margin 35.5%, PAT up only 3.5% YoY; sequential revenue flat on pharma and food lull.
524394|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income rose 9.9% YoY to INR1,149 million, with EBITDA up 10.5% to INR408 million at a 35.5% margin. Management said revenue was broadly flat QoQ, citing longer pharma customer decision cycles and a food-sample slowdown linked to Middle East disruption. PAT grew only 3.5% YoY to INR206 million (17.9% margin), with gross margin dipping on added capacity and higher material consumption. H1 FY27 total income was INR2,278 million (+11.8%), EBITDA INR819 million (+13.2%, 36% margin) and PAT INR417 million (+7.3%). The company remains net debt-free, with cash of INR701 million after taking INR15 crore of new long-term borrowing.

segments.name: Preclinical
segments.commentary: Management says it is among the largest growth drivers, with ~30% CAGR over the last four years; large-animal facility capacity constraint hit in H1 and is being expanded. Discovery work is mostly exports; safety/impurity work ~30-35%, all domestic.

segments.name: Clinical research (CRADS / BA/BE)
segments.commentary: Clinical research was weak in FY26 after losing major clients; BA/BE capacity fixed at 180 beds by choice. Contracts now with multiple customers; lead times 12-18 months; improvement expected in Q3-Q4. CT (clinical trials) had a lull after one large study.

segments.name: Biologics services
segments.commentary: Revenue generation began in Q2 FY27 with an initial booked order; revenue still very modest. About INR20-25 crore invested; talks with multiple clients, with management hoping to onboard a couple more this quarter. Ticket sizes INR100-125 lakh for process work; INR4-7 crore for lab-scale biosimilar development.

segments.name: Pharma analytics
segments.commentary: Top 5 or top 10 client share has ranged roughly 25-35% and varies by quarter; ~40% of pharma analytics revenue from overseas clients per slide. Management says large molecules are the future focus; peptides were strong last year.

segments.name: Food testing
segments.commentary: Export sample volumes fell sharply (e.g., 20-25 samples per shipment now down to 2-3). Import sample volumes at about 60-70% of normal, recovering from 30-40% in April-July. Shifting toward domestic clients.

segments.name: Electronics / EMI-EMC testing
segments.commentary: Stable QoQ with existing customers including defence OEMs, who use ~70-80% of Hyderabad capacity. EMI/EMC chamber capacity doubled after maxing utilisation; the business is small and volumes are episodic.

segments.name: Environment testing (PPM)
segments.commentary: Only PPM services offered; management will focus on higher-technology, higher-value PPM services.

524404|2026-03.headline: Marksans FY26 revenue rose 12.5% to INR2,951 crores with record PAT of INR420 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin hit 22.8%.
524404|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue grew 20.8% YoY to INR856 crores, with all three major regions growing and UK/EU posting its highest-ever quarter at INR308 crores. Q4 EBITDA rose 54% to INR195 crores, with margin up 491 bps to 22.8%, helped by mix, operating leverage and softer raw material costs in H2. Management flagged raw material inflation of 20-30% on petroleum-linked inputs for Q1 FY27, though it said inventory covers Q1 to a large extent. The company remains debt free with INR990 crores cash, a final dividend of INR0.90 per share was recommended, and FY27 guidance is 15-20% revenue growth with EBITDA margin in the 20-21% range.

524404|2026-06.headline: Marksans Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.6% YoY to INR841 crore, with record EBITDA of INR213 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT of INR159 crore.

Gross margin expanded to 59.1% on product mix, low-cost inventory and favourable FX, and EBITDA margin reached 25.3%. Management said the gross margin is sustainable at around 55-56% as freight and raw material costs from the war normalise, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin. Cash rose to INR1,058 crore, with net cash of INR1,031 crore after the QliniQ payment.

rows.why: Gross margin is guided to fall from 59.1% to 55-56% as the inventory benefit unwinds and freight and solvent costs stay high, and EBITDA margin must rise to 20-21% (21-22% year-end) from 25.3% in Q1, which the freight headwind could pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Germany is expected to generate revenue from early Q3 FY27 and Canada filings are underway, but no specific new product launches were named.

rows.label: Germany revenue start and Europe build-out
rows.why: Germany is expected to generate revenue from early Q3 FY27, with Europe guided to about INR180 crore for FY27 against Q1 Europe revenue of INR356 crore (incl. INR44 crore QliniQ) already run-rating.

rows.label: Inorganic deployment of INR1,031 crore net cash
rows.why: Net cash is INR1,031 crore and is earmarked for inorganic growth mainly in Europe, but management has nothing concrete yet and was non-committal on large M&A.

rows.label: US tariff and policy risk; no USFDA inspection timeline
rows.why: US is about 45% of revenue (INR377 crore), management has not committed to US manufacturing, and no definite timeline was given for the next USFDA inspection across three approved plants.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (revenue +35.6%, EBITDA +112.8%) and the US order book but cautious on forward gross margin (55-56% vs 59.1%), capital deployment and US manufacturing; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, gross margin normalisation and capital allocation of over INR1,000 cror

524494|2026-03.headline: Ipca Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 20.52% from 18.24%; FY27 guided to 12-13% growth and 1-1.25pp margin expansion.
524494|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR2,388 crores (up 6% YoY per the call's stated figure) and FY26 consolidated revenue of about INR9,646 crores (up 8%). Standalone EBITDA margin was 25.27% in Q4 (vs 21.19%) and 25.18% for FY26 (vs 22.66%). Management guided FY27 consolidated growth of 12-13% and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 22-22.3%, but flagged rising input costs (solvents, packaging, APIs) and freight costs linked to the Iran-US/Strait of Hormuz disruption. Unichem margins fell to about 8% and are guided to 12-13% for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +2.52pp vs 22.66% (stated as March '26 in call, FY25 implied)
+6% vs INR2,274 crores (call figure; FY26 and Q4 comparatives appear mixed in the transcript)

financial_highlights.metric: US business (Ipca USA + Unichem USA) Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.change: +10% vs INR388 crores in Q4 FY25
+12% vs INR764 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR853 crores (+12%); FY26 INR3,817 crores (+10%). Branded grew 14% in FY26, institutional fell about 24% to INR270 crores (Q4 INR74 crores vs INR111 crores). Ipca ranked 16th in MAT March '26 with 2.09% share (2.08% in Dec '25).

segments.name: Export formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 INR2,083 crores (+9%). Promotional branded exports grew about 14% to INR664 crores; generics ex-tenders grew about 17% to INR1,149 crores.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 INR1,396 crores (+10%). Management said API price increases are being passed through to buyers.

segments.name: US (Ipca USA + Unichem USA)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR428 crores (+10%); FY26 INR1,567 crores (+14%). Unichem US expected to grow about 10% in FY27; about 8 Ipca US generics marketed, 6-8 launches planned in FY27 by Ipca.

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin fell from about 12% to about 8% with flat turnover; Q4 other expenses rose by INR10-12 crores on tech transfers to third-party US manufacturers. Ireland facility closed; guided margin 12-13% in FY27.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and others
segments.commentary: Trophic Wellness (nutraceuticals) revenue about INR125 crores with profit about INR40 crores. Krebs Bio Nellore plant EBITDA positive; second plant has polishing issues. Onyx Scientific facing weak inquiry levels; UK formulation subsidiary lost INR2-3 million. Pisgah Labs formulation plant to be ready for commissioning around Q4 FY27, with meaningful turnover expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12-13% in INR terms (not currency-adjusted), with India and promotional markets at 12-13% and CIS at 10-11%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 22-22.3%, from 20.7% in FY26; standalone margin expansion guided at 1-1.25pp, below the earlier 1.5pp-plus norm due to material costs.
Domestic branded business guided at about 12% for FY27, with 1-2% from new products and the balance from price and volume.
Price increases of 6-7% expected in decontrolled domestic products; generic price increases are slower to pass through, with about 0.5-0.75% material cost impact expected.
Unichem FY27: US growth about 10%, EBITDA margin 12-13%.
Material costs could rise 10-12% if current petroleum prices persist; freight rose about 25% in Q4 and remains elevated.
capex_capacity: Pisgah Labs (US) formulation facility under construction; readiness for commissioning expected in Q4 FY27, with meaningful turnover in FY28.
Pisgah API facility reporting good order position.
Unichem Ireland manufacturing closed; production shifted to India; EUR 4-5 million annual overhead saving expected to stop in FY27.
Shipping mix changed at Unichem: air freight fell from about 40% a year ago to about 4-5% of shipments, adding some inventory in transit.
demand_pricing: Domestic branded growth driven by CIS and French-speaking Africa in exports, and pain, cardiac, derma, neuro and CNS in India.
Domestic institutional business fell on government funding constraints.
Solvent prices 40-50% above January levels; paracetamol and metformin prices up significantly; overall material cost up about 10-12% in the market.
Material cost to sales ratio about 25% for Ipca; management says input inflation can be offset by price rise and mix.
UK pricing was weak in FY26 but showing improvement with supply shortages.
Freight costs up about 25% in Q4; air cargo availability constrained and some shipments waiting 10-15 days.

qa_highlights.question: How many launches per year are needed to grow 15-20%, and what is the Q1-Q2 FY27 pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic launches of about 18-20 products a year across 20 divisions, with 2-3 power brands per division. US generics: 6-8 launches in FY27 for Ipca; Unichem 5-6. Europe and other markets: 3-4 generic launches per market per year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the US revenue and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated US revenue was INR428 crores in Q4 (+10%) and INR1,567 crores in FY26 (+14%). Management guided FY27 Unichem US growth of about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone material cost fell about 2% against roughly 10% growth for most of FY26. Margin gains came mainly from mix: domestic, ROW, cardiac, generics and API. Unichem's margin decline partly offset gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material and price outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs have risen sharply since February. Management expects 10-12% material cost inflation if petroleum prices hold, offset by 6-7% price increases in decontrolled products. Generic pass-through is slower, with about 0.5-0.75% material cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Unichem margins and inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guided at 12-13% for FY27, supported by closing Ireland, lower overheads and a US growth of about 10%. Inventory rose partly from a shift from air to sea freight (air fell from about 40% to 4-5%); management sees no concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Lyka Labs, Krebs Bio and other subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Lyka is an associate; management said profitability is lower as new animal health and critical care teams mature. Trophic Wellness had about INR125 crores revenue and INR40 crores plus profit. Krebs Nellore is EBITDA positive; the second plant has polishing issues. Onyx Scientific has weak inquiry levels.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (solvents, packaging, APIs) at 10-12% if petroleum prices stay high, with partial offset from price increases.
Freight and air cargo disruption tied to the Iran-US conflict and Strait of Hormuz; freight up about 25% in Q4 and expected to affect Q1 FY27.
Unichem margin recovery to 12-13% and inventory levels, given its US share losses and higher transit inventory.
Pisgah Labs formulation plant commissioning slipping from Q4 FY27 and Onyx Scientific's weak inquiry levels.
Domestic institutional business declining on government funding constraints (FY26 down about 24%).
Lyka (associate) profitability pressure from field force expansion.
524494|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin delivery, with a cautious note on near-term input cost and freight pressure. Management was candid on Unichem's weakness and subsidiary losses, but gave few specifics on Lyka and Onyx.

The improvement in overall margins is by and large because of product mix changes.
But I don't think so that will disturb my EBITDA margin significantly in the current year because, again, the product mix change and that's playing so overall, your margin.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided ~22-22.3% vs 20.7% in FY26 and standalone expansion 1-1.25pp, but material cost inflation of 10-12% if petroleum prices persist and generic pass-through is slower, with only 0.5-0.75% material cost impact flagged.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pisgah Labs US formulation facility is under construction with commissioning readiness expected Q4 FY27 and meaningful turnover in FY28, but no capacity utilisation or capex figures were disclosed and commissioning could slip.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated revenue guided 12-13% in FY27 with domestic branded ~12% (1-2% from new products, rest price and volume), US generics 6-8 launches and Unichem US ~10%; FY26 domestic formulations grew 10% and exports 9%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth 12-13% and margin 22-22.3%, with cost headwinds (material costs up 10-12% and freight up about 25% in Q4) capping upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight is expected to affect Q1 FY27 and petroleum-linked material inflation of 10-12% could persist, with Unichem margin needing to recover from about 8% to 12-13%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ipca plans 6-8 US generic launches in FY27 and about 18-20 domestic products a year across 20 divisions, with Unichem 5-6 US launches and 3-4 generic launches per market in Europe and other markets.

rows.label: Unichem Ireland closure saves EUR 4-5 million overhead
rows.why: Ireland manufacturing closed with production moved to India, and the EUR 4-5 million annual overhead saving is expected to stop in FY27, supporting Unichem margin recovery from about 8% to 12-13%.

rows.label: Price increases of 6-7% in decontrolled domestic products
rows.why: Management expects 6-7% price increases in decontrolled domestic products to offset 10-12% material inflation, with generic pass-through slower.

rows.label: Unichem margin recovery to 12-13%
rows.why: Unichem EBITDA margin fell from about 12% to about 8% on flat turnover and is guided to 12-13% in FY27, but inventory is elevated and tech transfer costs of INR10-12 crores hit Q4 other expenses.

tone.note: Management was confident on 12-13% growth and the margin path, and cautious on petroleum-linked input costs, freight and Unichem's weakness; the brief gives no analyst question detail beyond launches, US outlook, margin sustainability and raw materials.
